author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
Always inspect the task-local context when verifying before freeing. (#1462)

For some reason, the thread-bound context can become desynchronized
from the task-local one. Generally we don't notice this, because we
prefix every API call with a call that synchronizes both. Here, however,
we explicitly didn't to avoid initializing the state as that was thought
to cause the kind of initialization that may have to yield (which is
unsupported when done so from a finalizer).

However, just creating the task local state shouldn't result in yield,
only creating a stream does, like querying `active_state` as was done
before #1383.

239: Fix bug in gemm strided batched r=maleadt a=avik-pal

MWE:
```julia
using CuArrays
a = cu(rand(4, 3, 2))
b = cu(rand(3, 4, 2))
CuArrays.CUBLAS.gemm_strided_batched('T', 'T', a, b)
```

author: Sharan Yalburgi <sharanyalburgi@gmail.com>
message:
Add a dispatch for LinearAlgebra.norm2

`norm(@view x[..], 2)` was previously leading to a call of `LinearAlgebra.generic_norm2` which led to a scalar indexing. This catches such cuda subarray norm2 calls earlier.

Inf-norm and p-norm with cuda subarrays still lead to the following dispatches:
```julia
LinearAlgebra.generic_normInf(x) = float(mapreduce(norm, max, x))
LinearAlgebra.generic_norm1(x) = mapreduce(float ∘ norm, +, x)
```
I am not sure if there is a better way to dispatch the above.

should resolve https://github.com/JuliaGPU/CUDA.jl/issues/2280

message:
Don't assume host pointers are directly usable on the device.

Since CUDA.jl 3.4, we now always reconstruct a buffer object when
creating an array from a pointer. In the case of a HostBuffer,
that means we want the host pointer in the buffer object,
which is converted to a device pointer on request.

However, unsafe_wrap is invoked with a device pointer. Generally,
those pointers are identical, but on GPUs where
CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_USE_HOST_POINTER_FOR_REGISTERED_MEM==0,
that is not the case.

Instead, recover the host pointer from the device pointer passed to
unsafe_wrap. This is going back and forth between both pointer
representations, but those calls are reasonably cheap.

message:
Merge #286

286: use nvdisasm instead of cuobjdump r=maleadt a=vchuravy

`nvdisasm` provides more information by default, as an example function calls are resolved to the symbol instead of the pointer, and has a couple of useful options.
This defaults to printing available line information and only printing the code and not the data section.

The other options that are useful are:

- `--print-life-ranges`: Printing life ranges for registers
- `--output-control-flow-graph`: Get a CFG of the kernels

message:
Handle cache improvements (#2352)

Rework the handle cache so that handle ctors are dtors are known to the
cache. This makes it possible for it to evict handles at any time, and is
used to wipe handles when reclaiming memory.

Also switch to a spinlock to ensure safe operation in finalizers,
and consider collecting memory when allocating new handles.

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
Improve the build system.

This packs a couple of improvements:
- error out if ext.jl doesn't exist, otherwise the precompilation cache can become invalid (and doesn't update when ext.jl appears)
- support loading the package when build failed: this is useful for eg. building docs on Travis, or using the package conditionally (ie. only when a GPU is available)
- don't touch ext.jl when nothing changed, avoiding needless regeneration of the precompilation cache

message:
Merge #180

180: Fix sparse-dense matmul, with transposed dense r=maleadt a=irhum

Continuation of the pull request in https://github.com/JuliaGPU/CuArrays.jl/pull/728 

As previously mentioned, the patch makes sure the correct method is dispatched
```julia
# before the patch
densematrix_T = transpose(densematrix)
@which mul!(similar(densematrix_T, Float32, (size(sparsecscmatrix,1), size(densematrix_T,2))), sparsecscmatrix, densematrix_T)
# mul!(C, A, B) at stdlib/v1.4/LinearAlgebra/src/matmul.jl:208

# after the proposed patch
@which mul!(similar(densematrix_T, Float32, (size(sparsecscmatrix,1), size(densematrix_T,2))), sparsecscmatrix, densematrix_T)
# mul!(C::CuArray{T,2,P} where P, A::Union{CuArrays.CUSPARSE.CuSparseMatrixBSR{T}, CuArrays.CUSPARSE.CuSparseMatrixCSC{T}, CuArrays.CUSPARSE.CuSparseMatrixCSR{T}, CuArrays.CUSPARSE.CuSparseMatrixHYB{T}}, transB::Transpose{#s243,#s242} where #s242<:(CuArray{T,2,P} where P) where #s243) where T at CuArrays/l0gXB/src/sparse/interfaces.jl:20
```

and tests have been added for the sparse-transpose(dense) case as well

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
Remove eager synchronization with HtoD copies. (#2625)

We assumed unpinned memory would always synchronize, but that does
not seem to be the case. For some copy sizes (and potentially on
some, e.g. coherent, memory architectures) the copy is fully
asynchronous.

This optimization was made to make `CuRef` of a scalar fully async.
I considered making the `CuRef` ctor call `memset` instead, which
is always asynchronous by virtue of passing the memory by value,
however that does not support 64-bits floats while `memcpy` of
64 bits is still executed fully asynchronously.

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
When freeing memory, use the high-level device getter.

`current_device()` can throw an error when the current thread does
not have a context bound, and at the point we free memory there's
no guarantee that a context is bound: The preceding call to
`context()` only primes the *task* local state, and doesn't set
CUDA's *thread* local state. The latter is only set before any
API call that needs it, and `cuCtxGetDevice` is explicitly
exempt from that so that we can check whether a device is bound.

message:
Merge #301

301: Various improvements to docs r=maleadt a=timholy

I'm finally converting from old CUDArt to the newer infrastructure. I noticed a few places where I could help by improving the documentation. Now the only warnings when you include `make.jl` are related to `@ref`s to things like `InteractiveUtils.@code_llvm`, which AFAICT Documenter does not support.

The least satisfying part of this is the fact that I changed the "attachment point" for the documentation for `(::Kernel)(args...; kwargs...)`. The former choice was the most logical, but with a minute or two of experimentation I was unable to find a way to obtain that docstring from within the REPL. Consequently I moved it to the type itself, so that it can be obtained with `?CUDAnative.Kernel`.

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
Don't assume host pointers are directly usable on the device. (#1342)

Since CUDA.jl 3.4, we now always reconstruct a buffer object when
creating an array from a pointer. In the case of a HostBuffer,
that means we want the host pointer in the buffer object,
which is converted to a device pointer on request.

However, unsafe_wrap is invoked with a device pointer. Generally,
those pointers are identical, but on GPUs where
CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_USE_HOST_POINTER_FOR_REGISTERED_MEM==0,
that is not the case.

Instead, recover the host pointer from the device pointer passed to
unsafe_wrap. This is going back and forth between both pointer
representations, but those calls are reasonably cheap.

author: James Bradbury <jekbradbury@gmail.com>
message:
improved mapreducedim kernel

The algorithm here is to distribute 1024 threads/block among the inner
(reduction) and outer (map) dimensions; the remaining outer dimensions
get scheduled as the block grid. If fewer than 8 threads would be
dedicated to the inner dimension (because the outer dimension is much
larger) then we revert to the original kernel (which has the advantage
that it doesn't need to copy data to and from shared memory).

message:
When freeing memory, use the high-level device getter. (#2029)

`current_device()` can throw an error when the current thread does
not have a context bound, and at the point we free memory there's
no guarantee that a context is bound: The preceding call to
`context()` only primes the *task* local state, and doesn't set
CUDA's *thread* local state. The latter is only set before any
API call that needs it, and `cuCtxGetDevice` is explicitly
exempt from that so that we can check whether a device is bound.

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
Preserve 32-bit hardware indices, but use signed integers.

That way we keep the 32-bit width, without expensive checked conversions.

If we use 32-bit unsigned indices, operations like div or cld with an
64-bit signed integer argument (easily done using Julia's literals)
results in a 64-bit unsigned integer. Converting that to a 64-bit signed
integer (for arithmetic operations with other 64-bit signed integers,
again, likely from literals) requires checked conversions as the range
of 64-bit unsigned integers is larger than that of 64-bit signed ones.

By using signed 32-bit indices, operations like cld or div promote to
64-bit signed indices, avoiding subsequent conversions and thus
obviating checks.

message:
Merge #646

646: Improve mapreduce performance r=maleadt a=wongalvis14

~More than 3-fold improvement over the latest implementation~

Benchmarking function from https://github.com/JuliaGPU/CuArrays.jl/issues/611

First stage: Using the number of "max parallel threads a single block can hold" as the number of blocks, perform reduction with serial iteration if needed

Second stage: Reduction in a single block, no serial iteration

This approach aims to strike an optimal balance between workload of each thread, kernel launch overhead and parallel resource exhaustion.

```
New impl:
julia> @benchmark pi_mc_cu(10000000)
BenchmarkTools.Trial: 
  memory estimate:  16.98 KiB
  allocs estimate:  468
  --------------
  minimum time:     2.520 ms (0.00% GC)
  median time:      2.536 ms (0.00% GC)
  mean time:        2.584 ms (0.64% GC)
  maximum time:     15.600 ms (50.62% GC)
  --------------
  samples:          1930
  evals/sample:     1

Old recursion impl:
julia> @benchmark pi_mc_cu(10000000)
BenchmarkTools.Trial: 
  memory estimate:  17.05 KiB

Latest serial impl:
```

message:
Don't assume host pointers are directly usable on the device. (#1342)

Since CUDA.jl 3.4, we now always reconstruct a buffer object when
creating an array from a pointer. In the case of a HostBuffer,
that means we want the host pointer in the buffer object,
which is converted to a device pointer on request.

However, unsafe_wrap is invoked with a device pointer. Generally,
those pointers are identical, but on GPUs where
CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_USE_HOST_POINTER_FOR_REGISTERED_MEM==0,
that is not the case.

Instead, recover the host pointer from the device pointer passed to
unsafe_wrap. This is going back and forth between both pointer
representations, but those calls are reasonably cheap.

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
ND-reverse (#416)

* added reverse for arbitrary dimension CuArrays

* removed a redundant variable

* Simplified kernel

* Whitespace fixes.

* More compact testing.

* Clean-up reverse kernels.

* Drop specific typing.

* Unify kernels.

* Working, but non-coalesced in-place ND.

* Make the ND-case coalesced for 1D inputs.

* Unify in-place and out-of-place kernels.

Using shared memory for out-of-place is better since that enables memory coalescing on the output write.

* Drop the shared memory, use separate inplace/outofplace kernels.

Wrt. shared memory: newer hardware can coalesce both forward and backward access patterns,
which we would get without shared memory in the 1D case, while for the ND case we don't
get either of those if just writing backwards in the shared memory buffer.

Wrt. separate kernels: the in-place version would trample over values to be read by other blocks.
Grid synchronization is much to costly, so just swap numbers on half the number of threads.

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
Preserve 32-bit hardware indices, but use signed integers.

That way we keep the 32-bit width, without expensive checked conversions.

If we use 32-bit unsigned indices, operations like div or cld with an
64-bit signed integer argument (easily done using Julia's literals)
results in a 64-bit unsigned integer. Converting that to a 64-bit signed
integer (for arithmetic operations with other 64-bit signed integers,
again, likely from literals) requires checked conversions as the range
of 64-bit unsigned integers is larger than that of 64-bit signed ones.

By using signed 32-bit indices, operations like cld or div promote to
64-bit signed indices, avoiding subsequent conversions and thus
obviating checks.

cuDNN: only choose conv algorithms if they match descriptor mathType

This meant the `cudnnConvolution*` functions were seeing mismatches between descriptor math type and supported algorithm math types.

message:
Add Parallel Predicate Evaluation (count, and, or) and Tests - LLVM IR

`sync_threads_count(predicate)` (2 methods) for `llvm.nvvm.barrier0.popc(i32)`;
`sync_threads_and(predicate)` (2 methods) for `llvm.nvvm.barrier0.and(i32)`;
`sync_threads_or(predicate)` (2 methods) for `llvm.nvvm.barrier0.or(i32)`

`predicate` could be either
- `Bool` (returns `Bool`, or `Int32` for count) or
- `Int32` (returns `Int32`)

Future work:
1. As Valentin Churavy's comment suggests, a `% Bool` truncates a `Int32` to `Bool`. This runs well without unexpected behaviours in simple tests and real applications. But just to be safe, use `ifelse()`.
2. As Tim Besard commented, a more user friendly output could be of type `Int`: Although `Int` is now host dependent, "we've been doing that for `threadIdx` in the assumption that we'd be able to switch that to a GPU-native type at some point. It also makes it easier for LLVM to reason about integer arithmetic, since most values (literals, indexing, etc) is dealing with CPU-native Int already."

358: Add Synchronisation Barriers (count, and, or) r=vchuravy a=qin-yu

Added the following three intrinsics in `src\device\cuda_intrinsics\synchronization.jl`:
- `sync_threads_count(pred)` for LLVM IR `llvm.nvvm.barrier0.popc(i32)`;
- `sync_threads_and(pred)` for `llvm.nvvm.barrier0.and(i32)`;
- `sync_threads_or(pred)` for `llvm.nvvm.barrier0.or(i32)`.

and corresponding tests in `test\device\intrinsics.jl`.

_Although this is simple, I would like to express my special thanks of gratitude to Valentin Churavy and Tim Besard._

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
Remove eager synchronization with HtoD copies.

We assumed unpinned memory would always synchronize, but that does
not seem to be the case. For some copy sizes (and potentially on
some, e.g. coherent, memory architectures) the copy is fully
asynchronous.

This optimization was made to make `CuRef` of a scalar fully async.
I considered making the `CuRef` ctor call `memset` instead, which
is always asynchronous by virtue of passing the memory by value,
however that does not support 64-bits floats while `memcpy` of
64 bits is still executed fully asynchronously.

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
When freeing memory, use the high-level device getter. (#2029)

`current_device()` can throw an error when the current thread does
not have a context bound, and at the point we free memory there's
no guarantee that a context is bound: The preceding call to
`context()` only primes the *task* local state, and doesn't set
CUDA's *thread* local state. The latter is only set before any
API call that needs it, and `cuCtxGetDevice` is explicitly
exempt from that so that we can check whether a device is bound.

author: Tim Besard <tim@juliacomputing.com>
message:
Update the stream of libraries eagerly.

This makes stream switching take 500ns instead of 80, but it simplifies handle management
(making sure any active handles immediately use the new stream, reducing the risk of a
mismatch there), and avoids needless stream switches when switching tasks. The latter
seems like it might happen much more frequently, so it makes sense to have the overhead
when switching instead of when querying.

Furthermore, for KA.jl many APIs take stream arguments again, so it won't have to switch
streams globally anyway.

This PR makes it possible to generate a CUDAnative system image with GPU functions precompiled to LLVM IR. Initially, this makes it possible to more easily call back into Julia code from within the LLVM parts of CUDAnative, and eg. avoid code like https://github.com/JuliaGPU/CUDAnative.jl/blob/3f3ec236aa7cdfec4ba4186191691f5399f889d2/src/compiler/irgen.jl#L301-L320 (which required the ugly split from https://github.com/JuliaGPU/CUDAnative.jl/commit/1ec8d4378c63d35534e157127f0247def21ee9b9#diff-f5b4eae5039d79dd7ade646aae88e8fd). Instead, we can do regular LLVM-style calling like https://github.com/JuliaGPU/CUDAnative.jl/blob/7138bd73ace2c9bc4c832d94ba8bb19c0fab8944/src/compiler/irgen.jl#L308-L310 to regular functions like https://github.com/JuliaGPU/CUDAnative.jl/blob/7138bd73ace2c9bc4c832d94ba8bb19c0fab8944/src/device/runtime.jl#L47-L50 (with some magic to make it more usable)

message:
Always inspect the task-local context when verifying before freeing.

For some reason, the thread-bound context can become desynchronized
from the task-local one. Generally we don't notice this, because we
prefix every API call with a call that synchronizes both. Here, however,
we explicitly didn't to avoid initializing the state as that was thought
to cause the kind of initialization that may have to yield (which is
unsupported when done so from a finalizer).

However, just creating the task local state shouldn't result in yield,
only creating a stream does, like querying `active_state` as was done
before #1383.

message:
Merge #314

314: Implement PTLS and GC intrinsics r=maleadt a=maleadt

Attempt to fix https://github.com/JuliaGPU/CUDAnative.jl/issues/313 in a better way. Makes it possible to allocate on the GPU, and thus makes the following work:

```julia
@noinline custom_throw(x) = throw(x)
function kernel(i)
    if i > 0
        custom_throw(BoundsError())
    end
    nothing
end
```

This would previously allocate, since it isn't caught by the heuristic that catches throwing functions (a common pattern on 1.0 where GC frames are put in noinline functions not to spoil the hot path).

```llvm
define void @julia_kernel_1(i64) local_unnamed_addr {
top:
  %1 = icmp slt i64 %0, 1
  br i1 %1, label %L6, label %L3

L3:                                               ; preds = %top
  %2 = call %jl_value_t* @malloc(i64 16)
  %3 = addrspacecast %jl_value_t* %2 to %jl_value_t addrspace(10)*
  %4 = bitcast %jl_value_t* %2 to %jl_value_t addrspace(10)**
  store %jl_value_t addrspace(10)* null, %jl_value_t addrspace(10)** %4, align 8, !tbaa !1
  %5 = getelementptr inbounds %jl_value_t addrspace(10)*, %jl_value_t addrspace(10)** %4, i64 1
  store %jl_value_t addrspace(10)* null, %jl_value_t addrspace(10)** %5, align 8, !tbaa !1
  call fastcc void @julia_custom_throw_8317()
  call void asm sideeffect "trap;", ""() #0
  br label %L6

L6:                                               ; preds = %L3, %top
  ret void
}
```

Of course, with better analysis it should be possible to get rid of the allocation completely, but this is useful nonetheless.

WIP because it needs checked removal of the TLS getter.

author: bors[bot] <26634292+bors[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Merge #467

467: implement CuIterator for batching arrays to the GPU r=jrevels a=jrevels

I'm hitting what I believe is likely a common use case for CuArrays. My workload is essentially a map-reduce of the form:

```julia
some_reduction(f(batch::Tuple{Vararg{Array}})::Number for batch in batches)
```

Assuming `f` plays nicely with CuArrays, one way to get this running on a GPU is:

```julia
cubatches = (map(x -> adapt(CuArray, x), batch) for batch in batches)
some_reduction(f(cubatch) for cubatch in cubatches)
```

Unfortunately, this approach is a poor one when `batches` doesn't entirely fit in GPU memory. As the caller, I can assert that the old iterations' batches don't need to be kept around, so ideally, I'd have a mechanism to leverage to simply reuse old iterations' memory instead of allocating more. This PR implements such a mechanism: a `CuIterator` that maintains a memory pool and exploits the assumption that previous iterations' memory can be reused.

This is just a rough POC sketch right now just to express what I'm trying to get at...it's probably dumb in ways I can't yet comprehend. AFAICT I'd like to do the following before merging:

- [x] instead of the current shape/eltype-matching approach, just allocate to a device buffer (~`CUDAdrv.UnifiedBuffer`? I have no idea what I'm doing 😅 EDIT: oh is this how CUDAdrv exposes UVM or is that separate?~), increasing the buffer size as necessary once larger batches are encountered
- [x] ~leverage `CUDAdrv.prefetch` to asynchronously move values to GPU memory so as to not artificially block the iterator's consumer~ EDIT: I'm not sure this is necessary anymore assuming the `copyto!` call we're using is asynchronous?
- [x] make sure to free the pool once iteration is finished
- [x] docs
- [x] tests

In a future PR, we could add a feature for `CuIterator` to utilize UVM if the caller is in an environment where that's supported.

cc @vchuravy (thanks for discussing this with me earlier!)

message:
Infrastructure for multiple memory pools (#414)

Mostly NFC, but changes internal APIs and includes fixes to the binned memory pool,
the old implementation that is still used by default. Specifically, two issues, (a) the largest
pool would be inefficient (partially overlapping with the MAX_POOL cutoff) but
also potentially freeing pointers from it according to the large_alloc regime,
but worse (b) views would report the size of their allocation and thus size of
the object being freed as the size of the slice instead of the full array,
leading to potentially buffer being put in the wrong pool.

As <https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/cudnn/api/index.html#cudnnFindConvolutionBackwardFilterAlgorithmEx> notes, "Algorithms without the CUDNN_TENSOR_OP_MATH availability will only be tried with CUDNN_DEFAULT_MATH, and returned as such".
This meant the `cudnnConvolution*` functions were seeing mismatches between descriptor math type and supported algorithm math types.

message:
Remove magic from the infrastructure (warning: monolithic commit...)

This includes:
- no managed types (CuIn,CuOut,CuInOut), they were too costly anyway
- no bloated argument conversions as part of @cuda,
  just guess the appropriate kernel argument types and rely on Base.cconvert
- provide Base.cconvert for CuDevicePtr and CuArray
- make the lower-level launch() require users to provide to kernel argument types
- remove unused get_kernel_function()

Also fix some bugs:
- CuDim containing Int64
- CuDevicePtr args to cuLaunchKernel actually pointed to the entire CuDevicePtr object,
  which worked by chance as the inner Ptr is the first field
- properly split CuModule into CuModuleData and CuModuleFile

author: N5N3 <2642243996@qq.com>
message:
Update broadcast.jl

At present, `@cufunc` is able to generate a CUDA ver for existing function, like `Base.cis()`.  
However, if we want to use `@cufunc` for user defined functions, we must write the definition twice: first without `@cufunc`, then with it. This seems to be an unnecessary repetition.
On the other hand, if user only write the definition with  `@cufunc` , the const `_cufuncs` will be polluted, i.e.
```julia
julia> f
ERROR: UndefVarError: f not defined

julia> :f in CUDA.cufuncs()
false

julia> CUDA.@cufunc f(x) = x+1
ERROR: UndefVarError: f not defined
Stacktrace:
 [1] top-level scope at ~\.julia\packages\CUDA\dZvbp\src\broadcast.jl:110

julia> :f in CUDA.cufuncs()
true
```

This PR add a existence check and a name check.
1. If there's no existed method, then define a cpu version first.
2. If the function name is used as a variable, throw a error.
As there's no document for this macro, I'm not clear about the role of this macro in CUDA.jl. If i misunderstood its usage, just close this PR.

message:
Remove support for at-cuda calling precompiled CuFunctions.

This was sketchy anyway, as we didn't know the types the function was compiled for.
But worse, it was broken due to (what's probably a bug or yet another disallowed use
of) the generated function behind at-cuda: during the inference-stage execution,
it always dispatched to the implementation for F<:CuFunction, even though the argument
most definitely isn't a CuFunction (and runtime dispatch worked fine).

Due to lack of time to debug and upstream (and get an EWONTFIX) this, I've removed the code path.

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
rand: seed kernels from the host.

We should not (and cannot) rely on the fact that updating shared memory
will be visible across kernel launches. In some cases, it isn't, which
combined with pre-initialized shared memory (resulting in us not hitting
the make_seed path) causes identical values for the key and counters,
resulting in identical random numbers getting generated.

Avoid this by passing a seed from the host. Even in the case that updates
to counters don't survive to the next kernel, now the key will be different,
resulting in new numbers being generated.

author: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>
message:
Refactor memory wrappers (#2335)

This commit significantly reworks the CUDA.jl memory wrappers.

The low-level driver wrappers have been moved out of the Mem submodule,
and for consistency with Base the Buffer name has been replaced by
Memory. This is mostly an NFC change, and deprecations have been added
to make this non-breaking.

The high-level wrappers have been changed to to introduce a Managed
layer, i.e., CuArray now container a `DataRef` (from GPUArrays, for
refcounting), which contains a new `Managed`, which contains an
`AbstractMemory` subtype. The purpose of the `Managed` struct is to keep
track of the state of the memory, specifically, which stream has last
modified it, and whether there's outstanding asynchronous operations.
This information is used synchronize the memory when deriving a pointer,
making it possible to avoid explicit synchronization in many cases
(notably, when switching tasks or devices).

Sadly, this approach is not water-tight, notably, when memory is
captured (e.g. as part of a CUDA graph) we may not hit the pointer
derivation path and thus fail to synchronize. Explicit synchronization
is still required here, or an explicit copy to CPU memory (in which case
CUDA.jl will always synchronize).

As part of this change, several bugs and other minor issues were
discovered and fixed. Refer to the GitHub PR for an un-squashed version
of these changes for more details.

message:
Re-initialize the random seed every time.

Turns out we can't rely on the shared memory persisting across launches,
so we need to initialize the key at every launch. That also implies we
need a fresh seed for every launch, because otherwise two subsequent
launches would generate the same numbers. To avoid having to upload a
seed before every launch, use the `clock` register as a source of
randomness to initialize the key with.

message:
Merge #318

318: WIP: implement heap-allocated boxes r=maleadt a=maleadt

Implements `jl_box_uint64` which makes it possible to execute the following without our hacky `replace_throw!` pass:

```julia
function foo(i, ptr)
    for Ri_base in 0:1:i
        unsafe_store!(ptr, 0)
    end
    nothing
end
```

( this constructs a lot of boxes when creating exception objects )

Should also make it possible to eg. store into `CuArray{Any}` vectors, although it's pretty unclear there who owns that memory.

Additional difficulty: type tag values change across Julia sessions, so to avoid rebuilding the CUDAnative runtime each time I emit calls to `late_jl_uint64_type` and resolve those to actual values when linking the library.

Co-authored-by: Tim Besard <tim.besard@gmail.com>

message:
Merge #508

508: Add verbose option to code_sass r=maleadt a=thomasfaingnaert

This PR adds a `verbose` option to `@device_code_sass` and friends, which prints code generation statistics such as number of used registers, used constant memory, register spilling, ...

Example:
```julia
julia> function kernel()
           return
       end
kernel (generic function with 1 method)

julia> @device_code_sass @cuda kernel()
	.headerflags	@"EF_CUDA_TEXMODE_UNIFIED EF_CUDA_64BIT_ADDRESS EF_CUDA_SM75 EF_CUDA_VIRTUAL_SM(EF_CUDA_SM75)"
	.elftype	@"ET_EXEC"


//--------------------- .text.ptxcall_kernel_2    --------------------------
	.section	.text.ptxcall_kernel_2,"ax",@progbits
	.sectioninfo	@"SHI_REGISTERS=4"
	.align	128
        .global         ptxcall_kernel_2
        .type           ptxcall_kernel_2,@function
        .size           ptxcall_kernel_2,(.L_12 - ptxcall_kernel_2)
        .other          ptxcall_kernel_2,@"STO_CUDA_ENTRY STV_DEFAULT"
ptxcall_kernel_2:

.text.ptxcall_kernel_2:
        MOV R1, c[0x0][0x28] ;
        EXIT ;

.L_1:
        BRA `(.L_1);

.L_12:

julia> @device_code_sass verbose=true @cuda kernel()
ptxas info    : 0 bytes gmem
ptxas info    : Compiling entry function 'ptxcall_kernel_3' for 'sm_75'
ptxas info    : Function properties for ptxcall_kernel_3
    0 bytes stack frame, 0 bytes spill stores, 0 bytes spill loads
ptxas info    : Used 4 registers, 352 bytes cmem[0]
	.headerflags	@"EF_CUDA_TEXMODE_UNIFIED EF_CUDA_64BIT_ADDRESS EF_CUDA_SM75 EF_CUDA_VIRTUAL_SM(EF_CUDA_SM75)"
	.elftype	@"ET_EXEC"


//--------------------- .text.ptxcall_kernel_3    --------------------------
	.section	.text.ptxcall_kernel_3,"ax",@progbits
	.sectioninfo	@"SHI_REGISTERS=4"
	.align	128
        .global         ptxcall_kernel_3
        .type           ptxcall_kernel_3,@function
        .size           ptxcall_kernel_3,(.L_12 - ptxcall_kernel_3)
        .other          ptxcall_kernel_3,@"STO_CUDA_ENTRY STV_DEFAULT"
ptxcall_kernel_3:

.text.ptxcall_kernel_3:
        MOV R1, c[0x0][0x28] ;
        EXIT ;

.L_1:
        BRA `(.L_1);

.L_12:
```

message:
Fix value return for &FindPDBfile call

The script hangs in instances where it cannot find a pdb file referenced in a .hhr file (as it enters an infinite loop elsewhere in the code). This is because the &FindPDBfile() returns the name of the pdb file if it can find it. The file name should be tested at line. The original scripts fails to capture the return value of &FindPDBfile() so the test never occurs.

I have fixed line 1161 to correctly capture the return value.

Thus we can jump directly to the irep=1 entry in hitlist. message:
HMM::HMM() - initialize string arrays, MSAN issue

Although HMM::operator=() copyies the character arrays
in a safe way, with strmcopy(), Clang memory sanitizer detects
use of unitialized characters if the arrays are not initialized.
Just filling the first byte with '\0' is enough to fix this issue.

author: Dmitriy Samborskiy <samborsky_d@fastmail.com>
message:
backtraceMAC - fix errors in MAC algorithm

This commit introduces two checks in the MAC realignment algorithm
in order to alleviate Issue #153 ("MAC realignment algorithm damages hits",
https://github.com/soedinglab/hh-suite/issues/153):

1. If MAC hit is significantly shorter than the Viterbi
hit in terms of number of matched columns then the original Viterbi hit
is restored and an appropriate warning is issued.
This happens when MAC algorithm generates several disjoint local
hits or when MAC hit is shorter due to weak score at the start/end
regions of the Viterbi hit.
The threshold on the MAC hit length is defined by a new
option, -mac_min_length (default=0.9, i.e. at least 90% of number of
matched columns in Viterbi hit must be in the corresponding MAC hit).

There is no obvious way to deal with hit split in the current
MAC algorithm aproach, it is expected that the algorithm should
find the same Viterbi hit albeit improved and extended at its borders.
Usually the MAC hit restores its integrity as soon as the -mact
option is decreased. For example, in the test case described in the
issue report one could find the proper MAC hit if "-mact 0.33" is used
(instead of the default "-mact 0.35" value).
Therefore the warning also suggests decreasing -mact option as a viable
solution if MAC alignment is still needed.

Note: It would be nice to have support for "-mact auto" option
that forced the MAC algorithm to decrease -mact to the max. value
that restores the hit integrity (i.e. match the original Viterbi
hit to the degree defined by -mac_min_length option).

2. MAC realignment algorithm also can find a local hit that is
completely disjoint from the original Viterbi hit.
This possibility follows from the fact that viterbi_matrix
used in MAC DP algorithm is masked (see maskViterbiAlignment())
in a way that allows extension of the hit.
This commit adds a check that the found MAC hit has intersection
with Viterbi hit in both, query and target, coordinate spaces.
If the check fails, the alternative MAC hit that satisfies this
condition is sought (in decreasing score order).
When no valid MAC hit is found, the original Viterbi hit is restored
and an appropriate warning is printed.
This error was also observed in the reported issue, see the hit #4
(Score=11.3) that was mapped erroneously to the second part of
main hit, template columns [261; 357].

The alternative MAC hits' positions are collected in macAlgorithm()
procedure and later used in backtraceMAC() procedure.

author: Étienne Mollier <emollier@debian.org>
message:
src/a3m_compress.h: fix build failure with gcc 13

Following header changes in gcc 13, hh-suite fails to build with the
following errors:

	In file included from /<<PKGBUILDDIR>>/src/a3m_compress.cpp:8:
	/<<PKGBUILDDIR>>/src/a3m_compress.h:37:37: error: ‘uint16_t’ has not been declared
	   37 |   void writeU16(std::ostream& file, uint16_t);
	      |                                     ^~~~~~~~
	/<<PKGBUILDDIR>>/src/a3m_compress.h:38:28: error: ‘uint16_t’ has not been declared
	   38 |   void readU16(char** ptr, uint16_t &result);
	      |                            ^~~~~~~~
	[…]

Including cstdint in the affected file allows the build to go through.
This issue has initially been reported in [Debian bug #1037689].

[Debian bug #1037689]: https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=1037689

Signed-off-by: Étienne Mollier <emollier@debian.org>

author: Dmitriy Samborskiy <samborsky_d@fastmail.com>
message:
hhviterbialgorithm.cpp - fix ss_score_vec indexing

simd_float * ss_score_vec is an alias for float * Viterbi::ss_score array.
But use of ss_score_vec and ss_score is inconsistent in Viterbi::AlignWith*
procedures: initialization of ss_score is performed
from j=0 whereas ss_score_vec is indexed from j=1.
This leaves uninitialized the last positions of the array
which results in occasionally wrong values of SS score in the last
iteration of the inner loop (Vitrerbi + SS score = 1e+23) which in its
turn causes either crash at the attempt to construct hit alignment or
wrong hit outputs (huge score, zero E-value).

Unfortunately this error occurs only when several CPU cores are used
and even then it's not 100% reproducable (depends on the heap memory
layout which changes from run to run).

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Make paths relative to Git repo when adding files in wflow_commit.

If a file or directory no longer exists, git2r can't accept a relative
path to it. It requires an absolute path or a path relative to the
root of the Git repo.

This was discovered by Peter after the introduction of the feature of
removing unused figures. He had a file that had a figure but then had
zero. Since the directory no longer existed, if wflow_publish was run
from any directory other than the root, then the figure file was not
included in the commit. wflow_remove was designed to handle this since
it is always deleting non-existent files, but wflow_commit also needs
to be able to handle this.

https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/blob/a2fa789241d7245170043c07e5af00bd8ccd6b3b/R/wflow_remove.R#L169

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Output system info to R CMD check log.

Motivation: When testing on a remote server, I often don't have access
to the output files from R CMD check, e.g. the checks on CRAN servers
only report the file 00check.log. This makes troubleshooting very
difficult.

To get around this, I used the same strategy as the spelling package.
Each test file, e.g. test.R, creates an output file test.Rout in the
check output directory. However, if there exists a file test.Rout.save,
R CMD check prints the difference between the two files. The spelling
package does some more work to make the diff is minimal, but
for my purposes it is useful to also see the R commands, so I just have
the test script create a blank file for comparison.

https://github.com/ropensci/spelling/blob/807f4b64e3b4327bbca5fe6dce2822010827b027/R/spell-check.R#L172
https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Package-subdirectories

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Set httpuv as a dependency for use with wflow_use_github().

wflow_use_github() uses the httr package for oauth authentication
with GitHub. This is an important step specifically for novices
that may not be familiar/comfortable with GitHub. Unfortunately
httpuv is not automatically installed with workflowr because
httr lists httpuv as a suggested package, and has code to handle
this:

https://github.com/r-lib/httr/search?q=httpuv&unscoped_q=httpuv

If this were a developer-only focused package, I would do the
same. But the users that will rely on this the most need it
to simply be installed. Thus I listed it as a required dependency.

Supposedly RStudio Desktop requires httpuv 1.2.0 in order to
use the RStudio Viewer pane. However, I think this must be
context dependent. I uninstalled httpuv completely from my
Ubuntu machine running RStudio 1.2.1335, and I had no
problem using the RStudio Viewer pane.

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/08eb8fd120c3922e405d26074ee1f0c3a02cc5d1/src/cpp/session/modules/viewer/SessionViewer.cpp#L335

However, I couldn't get httpuv 1.2.0 to compile. Thus I
chose the oldest version that I could still compile,
which was httpuv 1.2.2. This makes sense since this is when
support for Rcpp 0.11.0 was added:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/httpuv/news/news.html

R CMD check doesn't complain about this dependency that it
doesn't look like I use. Presumably R 3.2.5 will complain since
it did about the methods package.

https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/commit/e159c4bf0219d811080dd169272fa6a8b07db8e6

But maybe they got rid of that NOTE because of use cases
like this. Who knows?

author: jdblischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Fix wflow_git_config() on Windows.

Related to Issue #76.

Git writes the global configuration settings to ~/.gitconfig. The
problem is that on Windows, ~ is mapped to ~/Documents. git2r is able
to use the settings in ~/Documents/.gitconfig, but Git will break at the
command line if ~/.gitconfig does not exist. If both exist, then git2r
uses the settings in ~/Documents/.gitconfig. The workaround is to create
an empty ~/.gitconfig first. git2r then writes to this file instead of
creating ~/Documents/.gitconfig.

https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/rw-FAQ.html#What-are-HOME-and-working-directories_003f

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
AppVeyor: Perform incoming CRAN checks that don't require remote access [skip travis] [skip circle]

The default setup uses the flag --as-cran but sets the envar
_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_ to FALSE. I hadn't realized this. Thus
it omits the folllowing checks:

* checking CRAN incoming feasibility
* checking use of S3 registration

However, since it still has --as-cran, it adds the following
checks:

* checking serialization versions
* checking for future file timestamps
* checking Rd line widths

Thus I manually set _R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_ to TRUE to include the
ommitted checks. However, I did set _R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_REMOTE_
to FALSE to avoid any spurious connection errors. This didn't show
any observable difference in the log file, but I suspect it skips
things like checking for valid URLs.

https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-ints.html#Tools
https://github.com/krlmlr/r-appveyor/blob/0aa11f8658e381c0d8647d46a58e21331534869c/r-travis/scripts/travis-tool.sh#L312

Note that _R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_ is also disabled by default on Travis:

https://docs.travis-ci.com/user/languages/r#environment-variables

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Specify the global environment when building R Markdown file in an
external R process.

Back story: The goal of build_rmd_external is to run render_site such
that it is completely isolated from the current R environment, similar
to how the RStudio "Knit" button works. This is an important feature for
reproducibility.

Matthew accidentally found an edge case where build_rmd_external and
RStudio Knit diverge. He had written a package function that referenced
a variable it hadn't defined inside the function, but it was defined
earlier in the R Markdown document that called the function. Using
RStudio Knit, the package function was able to access the variable
defined earlier in the R Markdown document. However, using
build_rmd_external via wflow_build, it failed due to the undefined
variable. This was good in Matthew's case, since it caught his mistake.
However, I want workflowr to behave identically to RStudio Knit or
manually running render_site in a new R session.

I wasn't sure how to fix this, but then I found this Issue on the
rmarkdown GitHub repo about using callr. The trick is to set the
environment to .GlobalEnv. This is slightly confusing, but it's not
referring to the global environment of the user, but the global
environment of the external R process that is started.

https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1204

created by wflow_build. It also needs to be committed by
wflow_publish, which fixes the old bug in #72 where the .nojekyll
file was not committed after changing the output directory.

message:
Fix AppVeyor-specific filepath issue.

The cache files created by knitr have very long names, thus these
cache files violate the max path length implemented in fs 1.3.2.
Furthermore, they can't be deleted with fs::dir_delete() or unlink().
Hence the new error in fs to alert the user to the cause of the issue.
unlink() fails silently. Thus when the on.exit() call tries to delete
the entire project directory, this will silently fail. Since each test
script creates a new project subdirectory, this shouldn't affect
anything. And this workaround is only done on AppVeyor.

Avoid NOTE from R CMD check.

wflow_use_github() requires httpuv::startServer() to be called
internally from httr to enable oauth authentication. Thus I
ensure it is installed by including it as an imported
dependency.

https://github.com/r-lib/httr/blob/6b84c576f866956e01835e1b6f02c55c8012d4e0/R/oauth-listener.r#L46

NOTE from R CMD check (e.g. on rhub but not win-builder):

* checking dependencies in R code ... NOTE
Namespace in Imports field not imported from: ‘httpuv’
  All declared Imports should be used.

which can be avoided by importing a function from that package
in the NAMESPACE.

https://community.rstudio.com/t/how-should-a-meta-package-handle-this-note-all-declared-imports-should-be-used/23400/3

Need to set interactive to true for code to be sent to R console. It's
not just for Shiny apps. interactive: false is for addins that affect

open file).

When I tried binding to workflowr::wflow_view, then it tried to execute
workflowr:::workflowr::wflow_view.

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Fix Windows-specific bug in the versions table.

I was using a path relative to the root of the Git repo. This should
work because in general git2r supports these types of input paths.
However, in this case, the relative path on Windows gets converted to
a non-existent absolute by path via commits() -> sanitize_path() ->
normalizePath(). Thus my solution is to pass absolute paths to
git2r::commits(), and then switch to relative paths for displaying
to users in the version table.

https://github.com/ropensci/git2r/issues/394#issuecomment-585989444

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Avoid false positive test failures for pandoc title warning.

The tests that check for pandoc warnings required the calls to be
absolutely silent. This is misleading since any random message sent to
stderr would cause the tests to fail, even though nothing had changed as
far as this behavior.

This was happening on the weekly build "future", which used a slightly
different strategy for installing system dependencies compared to the
"devel" build. As far as I can tell that is what caused the difference.

https://circleci.com/gh/workflowr/workflowr-pkg-tests/686

The warning came from grSoftVersion():

Warning message:
In grSoftVersion() :
  unable to load shared object '/usr/local/lib/R/modules//R_X11.so':
  libSM.so.6: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

I fixed it by installing libsm6 and then libxt6.

Once I confirm this test update fixes things, then I'll update the
"future" build so that it is more similar to the other builds.

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Update .Rbuildignore so that only files in the root of the repository
are ignored. Otherwise the template files in inst/infrastructure are
also removed when the package is built with `R CMD build`.

For an explanation on which files are removed, see the Writing R
Extensions manual:

https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Package-structure

To solve the isssue, I copied the strategy from devtools, which also has
template files in inst/.

https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/1ce84b04568ff7846c3da754f28e7e22a23c8737/.Rbuildignore

The .Rbuildingore file uses Perl-like regular expressions. I find
?regexp completely incomprehensible. The link below was much more
straightforward.

. -> match any one character
.* -> match any character zero or more times
\. -> An actual period
^ -> beginning of string
$ -> end of string

https://www.cs.tut.fi/~jkorpela/perl/regexp.html

The .nojekyll file survives the build process, but not .gitignore. It'd
probably just be easier to create it from scratch.

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Use utils::packageVersion() according to examples in documentation.

utils::packageVersion() returns an object with classes
package_version and numeric_version. The examples in the documentation
compare the results to a character vector, e.g. "1.5".

In workflowr, I had been using this and various other methods.

Sometimes I compared directly to a number. This worked only because
R is forgiving, e.g. `1 == "1"` returns TRUE. While it worked, I
don't like relying on such unintuitive behavior.

Sometimes I compared it to the class numeric_version, e.g.
as.numeric_version("1.5"). This seems overly cautious, since even
the examples don't suggest this is necessary.

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Require stringr >= 1.3.0 to prevent wflow_start() infinite recursion
error.

I remember seeing this error at the BSD workshop back in April 2019,
but had no idea what was causing it. I happened to reproduce it
when in the RStudio Server hosted in the Docker image rocker/verse
(I wanted to test the httpuv error with the Viewer pane). I got
the same error message as some of the students:

wflow_start("test")
Error: evaluation nested too deeply: infinite recursion /
options(expressions=)?
Error during wrapup: evaluation nested too deeply: infinite recursion /
options(expressions=)?

It happened no matter the directory, or using the RStudio project
template.

The error was caused by the recursive function
obtain_existing_path(). It didn't have a stop criteria if it was
passed nonsense like NA, so it went on recursively until it errored.

The NA came from absolute() -> toupper_win_drive(). stringr 1.2.0
introduced the ability to use a function to perform the replacement.
This is how toupper_win_drive() works, it uses toupper. The problem
is that if there is no match, instead of returning the original
string, it returns NA.

This was fixed in stringr 1.3.0 in PR #164. The NEWS bullet is
quite subtle for how much it changes the behavior.

https://github.com/tidyverse/stringr/pull/164

message:
Trying to troubleshoot wflow_git_commit() on winbuilder.

All the current problems appear to be caused by wflow_git_commit() not
adding files. When wflow_git_commit() first receives the file names, it
converts them to relative paths. Prior to adding with git2r::add(), it
converts them to absolute paths (which is required for deleted files or
directories). Then git2r::commit() fails because no files were added.
Thus something must be breaking the files paths during the conversion
from relative -> absolute.

for (x in c("tests/testthat/test-git2r-merge.R",

  lines_out <- stringr::str_replace(lines_in,

  writeLines(lines_out, con = x)
}

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
More winbuilder exerpimenting. [skip ci] [ci skip]

What I learned:

* fs::dir_exists() returns FALSE if the directory has a trailing slash.
This only happens on winbuilder. It doesn't occur on my local Windows 10
machine or on AppVeyor. This is what was causing the errors with
wflow_rename()/wflow_use_gitlab(). These involve
renaming a directory and the early check with fs::dir_exists() would
fail.

* The tests are run in
d:/RCompile/CRANguest/R-release/workflowr.Rcheck/tests_x64/testthat
and the temporary directory is D:/temp/RtmpoNs5r5/file7cb017ec743. They
are both on the D drive, but notice the difference in the case of the D
drive. Both getwd() and fs::path_wd() return the current working
directory with a lower case d.

* workflowr:::relative() appears to return the correct relative path
from the test directory to a temporary file. It goes up 6 levels to D:/
and then goes forward starting with temp/, e.g.
../../../../../../temp/RtmpoNs5r5/file7cb027113cf9. I think this is the
correct relative path because fs::file_exists returns TRUE.

* fs::path_rel() does not appear to return the correct relative path to
a temporary file. It goes up 7 directories and then starts with D:/.
Basically it behaves as if there is a root above all the drives,
e.g.  ../../../../../../../D:/temp/RtmpoNs5r5/file7cb017ec743. I think
this is incorrect because fs::file_exists() returns FALSE. The problem
appears to arise from the fast that fs::path_wd() returns d:/ and
fs::file_temp() returns D:/, and then fs::path_rel() doesn't recognize
that these are identical on a case-insensitive file system like Windows.

* Because wflow_git_commit() starts by converting the files to relative
paths, this is likely causing the problems on winbuilder. I like
returning relative paths to the user, so I need to try to keep the paths
absolute as much as possible expect for message and return() statements
to see if this improves the situation. The problem will be
wflow_publish() which calls wflow_git_commit() and wflow_build().

* R.home() is D:/RCompile/recent/R-35~1.2

* fs::path_home() is C:/Users/CRAN

* fs::path_home_r() is C:/Users/CRAN/Documents

* wflow_update() fails because _workflowr.yml is not committed. It is
still an untracked file. Maybe this is because it is the only file that
is completely new to Git? All the others are being modified or deleted.

* wflow_use_gitlab() fails because it commits .gitlab-ci.yml (a new
file) but not analysis/_site.yml (an existing file). The variable
output_dir had been changed to ../public, so it should have had changes
to be committed with Git.

* wflow_use_github() fails when wflow_publish() is run afterwards.
wflow_git_commit_ claims there are no HTML files to commit. Running
wflow_build() beforehand confirmed that the Rmd files are built. Maybe
it is looking for the HTML files in the wrong directory? Or maybe
relative paths are causing problems?

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Create git2r_add to handle all edge cases.

git2r::add() is a constant source of frustration because the file paths
it accepts depend on various combinations of factors that behave in
unpredictable ways.

Paths can be passed in multiple ways: 1) relative to the current working
directory, 2) relative to the Git directory (which isn't always the same
as the former), and 3) absolute paths.

The following affect which type of path can be used:

* Operating system, especially Windows.

* Whether the file is being modified, deleted, or added for the first
time. wflow_update() was failing because it added the modified files
but couldn't add the untracked file _workflowr.yml. A deleted file can't
be added with 1). It has to be relative or absolute. The motivation for
the commit below was to allow wflow_remove() to reliably remove files
from the Git repo.

https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/commit/c28bf02067d0941c877ae9866849317fbf5ae3da

* The version of git2r or libgit2. This has changed over time. The
commit above solved the problem for the previous release, and it stil
works for the most part. It mainly just choked on winbuilder.

* Arguments like "." have a special meaning (git add .), so shouldn't be
altered.

This was discovered during the UChicago QBio workshop. Users expected
wflow_publish() to behave similar to wflow_build(), in that it would
automatically do what it needed without explicit direction. Since
publishing a file is much hard to undo than building it, users need to
explicitly specify the files to publish. Since there is no use case for
running wflow_publish() without instructing it to publish some files, I
updated it to fail early in this situation. The only way to obtain the
old behavior is to set dry_run=TRUE.

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Make add_bibliography() tests more flexible. For some reason, rmarkdown 1.7 with pandoc 2.7 added a role attribute to the refs div tag. This broke the regex that searched the HTML for the position of this bibliography.
I didn't need to change the code. Pandoc still expects the user to manually include
to specify a location for the bibliography. At least as far as I can tell. I tried manually assiging the role attribute, and this resulted in pandoc then adding a duplicate refs div but with a class attribute.
If I updated add_bibliography() to use a more flexible regex and manually added the role attribute, then pandoc added a duplicate role attribute. Thus I think it is clear that this shouldn't be added by the user. And thus doesn't need to be detected by workflowr. This is an edge case anyways, for users that manually added a bibliography before this was supported by default.

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Remove git2r_slot() for S4 support.

This required a crazy regex with 2 capture groups. I tried for a
while but wasn't able to pass the regex to `sed -E` via my bash
script sed.sh. So eventually I just ran it manually.

Note that -E enables extended regular extensions, so I don't
have to backslash-escape the capture group parentheses.

Examples:

from: sha <- git2r_slot(log[[1]], "sha")
to:   sha <- log[[1]]$sha

from: files <- sapply(git_diff$files,
to:   files <- sapply(git2r_slot(git_diff, "files"),

for f in R/*R tests/testthat/*R
do
  echo "Editing file $f"
  sed -i -E -e s/'git2r_slot\(([^"]+), "([^"]+)"\)'/'\1$\2'/g $f
done

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Use -- to denote files in call to `git log`.

Required to avoid ambiguity when a file doesn't exist (b/c then
Git isn't sure if it is a revision or a file).

For example, without the --, deleting docs/index.html and then
running `git log` generates the following error:

$ git log -n 1 docs/index.html
fatal: ambiguous argument 'docs/index.html': unknown revision or
path not in the working tree.
Use '--' to separate paths from revisions, like this:
'git <command> [<revision>...] -- [<file>...]'

message:
Pin rocker/r-ver:devel to the version from 2 weeks ago.

The devel image was recently updated to use Debian 10 (buster)
and then libicu63.

https://github.com/rocker-org/rocker-versioned/commit/b1d2b1b1f8b338b66fb8f855899413a36ac60462#diff-8e87d872cd4b82b711d6ad5bc2fc01c9

This causes littler to crash unexpectedly (it doesn't mention that
it depends on icu):

r: error while loading shared libraries: libicuuc.so.57: cannot open
shared object file: No such file or directory
Exited with code 127

I am pretty sure this is due to the cache being outdated. stringi
is built with libicu57 and not libicu63, which is what is installed.
Unfortunately there is no way to automatically invalidate the cahce
due to an OS update:

https://support.circleci.com/hc/en-us/articles/360004937834-Resolving-Ruby-Jessie-to-Stretch-issue-cannot-open-shared-object-file-cache-problem

I'm still a little confused why Rscript worked but not littler,
since the latter does not appear to rely on icu. Unclear why it
would be trying to load stringi.

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Detect absolute paths in strings.

Will be used in a reproducibility check for wflow_html().

The difficulty is in allowing spaces in file paths, which complicates
the regular expressions. I had to anchor them by requiring they be
surrounded by quotations marks, e.g. a string in the R code, or by
parentheses, e.g. a link in Markdown syntax.

Even this didn't allow finding multiple absolute paths on the same line.
Getting this to work required changing .+ to the non-greedy .+? to stop
at the first appearance of the next quotation mark or parentheses.

https://stackoverflow.com/a/171483/2483477

author: John Blischak <jdblischak@gmail.com>
message:
Use raw date format for backwards compatibility with Git.

The data format "unix" was added in Git 2.13.7. My Ubuntu has
2.17.1. However, rocker/r-ver:3.2.5 has 2.1.4, causing an error.

https://github.com/eamodio/vscode-gitlens/issues/860#issuecomment-533953146

Thus I instead use the raw date format and then parse it to only
obtain the first part containing the unix time.

$ git log -n 1 --date=unix --format=%ad
1576601494
$ git log -n 1 --date=raw --format=%ad
1576601494 -0500

message:
Check minimum required versions of dependencies. See #178

Interestingly, this isn't needed for knitr. If there is an outdated
version of knitr, R automatically throws an error upon attaching
or install.packages()

> library(workflowr)
Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘workflowr’ in
loadNamespace(j <- i[[1L]], c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck =
vI[[j]]):
 namespace ‘knitr’ 1.16 is being loaded, but >= 1.22 is required

I don't know why. In contrast, git2r and rstudioapi can have outdated
versions, and R is silent.

The error was occurring when the F.interpolate function was called with new_height and new_width as arguments for the size parameter. These variables were of type numpy.intc, while F.interpolate expected arguments of type int or Tuple[int] or Tuple[int, int] or Tuple[int, int, int].

The fix involves converting new_height and new_width to Python's native int type before they are passed to F.interpolate. This ensures that the function receives arguments of the correct type, preventing the TypeError.

message:
Refactor after conversation with Max

Had a video call with Max to verify the fidelity of the py model to the
original excel model. Found a few inconsistencies.

Changed r0 to r. r0 is the initial value of r.

Added a couple of static variables, and changed
case_fatality_rate_hospitals_overwhelmed and
rolling_intervals_for_current_infected to be calculated from those
vairables at the start of the model execution. Max felt it was a more
faithful representation of reality.

Isolated the way we determine if a hospital is overloaded and the way we
calculate 'effective' r. Doesn't make a huge difference now, but will
make it easier to maintain and update in the future.

message:
Long term fix for build_api_v2_test (#1066)

This PR adds a small stable subset of timeseries data to use in tests that have in the past used the entire combined_datasets. It build on https://github.com/covid-projections/covid-data-model/pull/1064 that made reading and writing to different file paths easier.

With this change running all the non-slow tests (as done by `make test-fast`) takes 23 seconds instead of almost a minute and the longest duration non-slow test dropped from 28 seconds to 1.1 second.

This change will prevent data updates breaking our fast tests. The slow tests can still be broken but these are generally more stable.

`./run.py data update-test-combined-data` updates the data.

message:
rm DataSource FIELD_MAP constants (#916)

This PR addresses https://trello.com/c/uPQXBuDg/777-remove-unused-datasource-constants

## This PR

This PR changes most DataSource subclasses to be just a few constants without custom code. The exceptions are sources that produce static data or make some custom tweak to the produced dataset.

* Removes `DataSource.local()` which created in intermediate DataFrame that is no longer useful.
* Replaces calls to `data_source_cls.local().multi_region_dataset()` with `data_source_cls.make_dataset()`
* Removes `DataSource.INDEX_FIELD_MAP` and `DataSource.COMMON_FIELD_MAP` which stopped being useful when we started doing the transformations in the covid-data-public repo
* Adds constants `DataSource.EXPECTED_FIELDS` `DataSource.COMMON_DF_CSV_PATH` and `DataSource.IGNORED_FIELDS` that are used in the default `make_dataset` to load timeseries data

## Tested

Ran `./run.py data update`. `dir -lrt data/multiregon*` shows the files were re-written recently and `git status` shows they are not modified from the main branch.

message:
MultiRegion regional attributes (#797)

## This PR

* Instead of calculating the latest value for each timeseries before combining data do it when the latest value is read from MultiRegionDataset
* Replace MultiRegionDataset data (geo data and timeseries together) and latest_values (timeseries latest values and constants such as population together) with `timeseries` (only timeseries of numeric values) and `static` (geo data and constants)
* Remove NEW_CASES logic for updating latest values, which is no longer needed.
* add parameter to_csv(write_timeseries_latest_values) to help with testing
* Add backports.cached_property and use it for non-trivial properties


## Testing

Manually set to_csv(write_timeseries_latest_values=True), ran `python ./run.py data update` and then `git difftool -t vimdiff data/multiregion.csv` to see what changed. This showed that county and state data was identical using the new latest value logic as the old logic. CBSA recent values changed, probably because aggregation is broken, but not an issue because these regions are in beta; fixing them is my next task and will be easier after this is in.

I ran built snapshot in this branch using the same data as a recent master snapshot. https://covid-projections-git-bump-snapshot-1316-326.covidactnow.now.sh/internal/compare/?left=1336&locations=2&metric=3&right=1335&sort=3 shows no differences in any timeseries produced for the website.

author: Brett <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Ensure a Snapshot is Sent to the Github Action Runner as a Single Unit of Work

Enforce a queue to the GitHub self-hosted runner that treats the creation of the entire snapshot as the job.

The previous version separated the workflow into multiple "jobs" that were linearly dependent on each other. That "jobs" abstraction is built to allow parallel processes, and if we used the GitHub hosted version it would run up to 20 jobs in parallel. However, the runner built for self-hosting prioritizes the jobs across snapshots in a way that delays the time to first snapshot completion (without changing the time to last snapshot completion). Instead of completing all the jobs of the first snapshot, it will cycle through each outstanding snapshot request calling the next available job for that snapshot.

It is better to have the early snapshot complete and unblock the person waiting for it.

This is solved by switching a given snapshot to a single job with multiple steps. The "steps" abstraction is the correct mental model that enforces sequential ordering (which we want anyways in our current implementations). So this will send all the commands to the runner as one packet.

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Fix ICU Utilization Metric When Incorporating New 'Cumulative ICU' Datastream (#427)

Updated the 'estimate current number of hospital/icu beds occupied' by improving the model initialization and removing some unplanned sources of variability.

* ICU Estimation from Cumulative ICU Data

Improve the estimation of current icu covid patients in the case where we are only provided with cumulative icu patients.

Sometimes covidtracking provides cumulative, but not current, data for hospitalization and icu. We then estimate the number of patients currently in the ICU. There are multiple things with this implementation that need to be improved, however they can be done in stages. The first stage is to standardize the calculation of ICU. Right now the estimate uses a variable drawn from a wide distribution (roughly 8.6 +/- 2.6 days). This introduces a large source of noise in the snapshot to snapshot calculations. In other places this code is usually called multiple times and then averaged, but for here it is just called once. Instead of bumping up the call/average, I just calculated the value from the means. The consistancy day-to-day is key, especially since this parameter isn't used in any monte-carlo modeling.

I left the hospitilization branch still drawing from the distribution, but averaging over 250 samples. Timeit shows an increase from 8.4ms to 27.2ms. If this becomes significant, we can refactor the params code and surface this constant.

Finally, our new linter just came online, so there will be misc line cleanups for a bit.

* Parameter Scope Reduction for Temporary Test

The added parameter tripped up code elsewhere that has a script list of allowed keys. This constant is now local, but will be incorporated into the params later.

* Refactoring Current_To_Cumulative Code

Trying to isolate the code that converts current to cumulative from the code that just loads any data.

* Refactored Current to Cumulative Outside Load Data

Extracted the logic to convert cumulative totals to an estimate of current patient population. Before this, it was added into a data loading function as an optional flag. That structure was too constraining to include required features of the model (i.e. requiring more than one value provided to extrapolate from).

* Documentation and Reformatting

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
GitHub Self-Hosted Runner Queue (#514)

Ensure a Snapshot is Sent to the Github Action Runner as a Single Unit of Work

Enforce a queue to the GitHub self-hosted runner that treats the creation of the entire snapshot as the job.

The previous version separated the workflow into multiple "jobs" that were linearly dependent on each other. That "jobs" abstraction is built to allow parallel processes, and if we used the GitHub hosted version it would run up to 20 jobs in parallel. However, the runner built for self-hosting prioritizes the jobs across snapshots in a way that delays the time to first snapshot completion (without changing the time to last snapshot completion). Instead of completing all the jobs of the first snapshot, it will cycle through each outstanding snapshot request calling the next available job for that snapshot.

It is better to have the early snapshot complete and unblock the person waiting for it.

This is solved by switching a given snapshot to a single job with multiple steps. The "steps" abstraction is the correct mental model that enforces sequential ordering (which we want anyways in our current implementations). So this will send all the commands to the runner as one packet.

message:
agg vaccine percentages using population weights (#928)

This PR addresses https://trello.com/c/WYdvQgl4/865-metro-vaccinated-incorrect

### Tested

Without this change the data the percentage is obviously broken:

```
$ csvgrep -c location_id -m cbsa:12580 data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv  | csvgrep -c variable -r 'vac.+pct' | csvcut -c 1-10
location_id,variable,provenance,2021-02-03,2021-02-02,2021-02-01,2021-01-31,2021-01-30,2021-01-29,2021-01-28
iso1:us#cbsa:12580,vaccinations_completed_pct,,12.397,12.397,,,,,
iso1:us#cbsa:12580,vaccinations_initiated_pct,,57.552,57.552,,,,,
```

Updating my local covid-data-public repo, then running `./run.py data update`.

With this fix:
```
csvgrep -c location_id -m cbsa:12580 data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv  | csvgrep -c variable -r 'vac.+pct' | csvcut -c 1-10
location_id,variable,provenance,2021-02-03,2021-02-02,2021-02-01,2021-01-31,2021-01-30,2021-01-29,2021-01-28
iso1:us#cbsa:12580,vaccinations_completed_pct,,1.808496,1.808496,,,,,
iso1:us#cbsa:12580,vaccinations_initiated_pct,,7.983439,7.983439,,,,,
```

Looking at `git difftool --no-prompt -t vimdiff main -- data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv` is see only changes in ..._pct metrics in 9 CBSAs.

message:
Refactor Infer_Rt Step 2 (#530)

This PR is the first part of a refactor for our rt inference code.

The infer_rt code now has its own submodule, and has been refactored to accept data agnostic to the aggregation level. This submission does not change any of the major internal components. It just structures the infer_rt code in its own submodule and pulls apart the RtInferenceEngine class into more manageable chunks. Now that Alex's significant improvements have landed, it's time to pay down that technical debt while allowing us to investigate new aggregation levels.

This change is in support of refactoring the inputs into RtInferenceEngine to be agnostic to aggregation level, which will allow for more manageable testing, maintenance, extensibility, and readability. Also, the tests for infer_rt are now under the same file in the test dir.

Outstanding Changes Remaining:
- A change to make the test correction more responsive to data from the last week was removed and will be put as a separate PR.
- Chris made some good recommendations about how to change the internal structure of the code, which will be a separate PR.
- Cli revamps to call a just the infer rt code was separated as a separate PR.
- The whitelist for pyseir and for infer_rt should be completely separated.


* initial commit from stash

* tail suppression addressed, compared with rt.live and inference unit tests working

* generate snapshots for this branch

* fixed breaks caused by merge from master

* first pass at modifying test volume adjustment - not working well yet

* Move infer_rt to Separate Submodule

* ready for Brett made sure all tests working

* Remove Hospitalization Data References from Infer RT

* Remove Cross Dependency on Pyseir Parameter Generation

Note: The serial period is now fixed in InferRtConstants instead of estimated from pyseir. I think it's reasonable to maintain these separately.

* Enforce RtInferenceEngine Accesses InferRtConstants Only Through Init

First step to isolate cross dependencies on the infer_rt script. Most of these should be class variables instead of instance variables, but that's for another time. Right now the goal is to make it clear that everything in the RtInferenceEngine is self contained.

* Extract Plotting Boilerplate to Separate File

* Pull Data Loader out of RtInferenceEngine

Make the core Infer Rt Code Agnostic to the Aggregation Level.

* Remove Import Rename in CLI by Renaming Fun

As per PR#530, we are simplifying the Bettencourt Rt inference work. Part of that work was making a separate submodule. The cli api was inconsistent about calling this method (all the other ones prepend run_). This change fixes that inconsistency. It will break old api calls that directly called infer_rt (instead of run_infer_rt). The cli is almost exclusively used internally, so I think this change is worth the possible confusion, especially because it will fail loudly and quickly.

The infer rt tests now use the new method of passing in a dataframe. All tests pass, but I think that's more a function of bad test coverage. Especially around initialization. A good opportunity to create more tests!

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
synthesize testing data for valorum (#616)

## This PR

https://trello.com/c/mIImJgh5/282-consume-plumb-test-positivity-data-for-louisiana-counties-from-valorum

* Adds `CovidCountyDataDataSource.synthesize_test_metrics` that generates testing data where they can be calculated from other metrics and keeps method used to generate it in provenance.
* Adds optional `DataSource.provenance`, with same structure as `TimeseriesDataset.provenance`
* Any DataSource with provenance (currently only Valorum/CovidCountyDataDataSource) is written to disk in a wide-dates.csv
* Factors out `wide_dates_df.write_csv`
* Extends `run.py utils csv-diff` to support the left side being a git rev, ie `run.py utils csv-diff master data/timeseries.csv`
* Sorts csv-diff output of timeseries by amount of diff because nobody cares about metrics that haven't changed.
* Changes ` _to_timeseries_rows` (turns a provenance DataFrame with a string for every date to a string per variable) to join all values with `;` instead of keeping only the first. And renamed it to `provenance_wide_metrics_to_series`
* Changes the contents of `build_us_with_all_fields` to be inlined at the one calling site.


## Tested

I ran `./run.py data update` and then `./run.py utils csv-diff master data/timeseries.csv` to find out how the combined data changed. There are 574 FIPS that gained a negative_tests metric. negative_tests and positive_tests changed for lots of FIPS. Here are the top 20:
```
                          diff  points_overlap  has_overlap
variable       fips                                        
negative_tests 36061  1.000000             205         True
positive_tests 48431  0.714286              14         True
               17031  0.408864             151         True
negative_tests 17031  0.374730              37         True
positive_tests 48451  0.207374              14         True
               48135  0.189428              14         True
               48093  0.141138              14         True
               48355  0.126038              14         True
               48149  0.104994              14         True
               48465  0.094098              14         True
               01121  0.058504             157         True
               01009  0.045378             155         True
               01039  0.045270             154         True
               48449  0.041463              14         True
               17091  0.036001             151         True
               01099  0.033007             149         True
               01019  0.029950             156         True
               01053  0.026612             152         True
               01115  0.024237             150         True
               01057  0.023739             150         True
```

36061 is NYC! Looking at `grep -P -H '\A36061,negative_tests' data-af258b1/timeseries-wide-dates.csv data/timeseries-wide-dates.csv` where af258b1 is master we had all `0` for negative_tests from Valorum. I don't know why it was 0 and looked at the covid-data-public repo `csvgrep -c fips -r '(36047|36081|36005|36085|36061)' data/cases-covid-county-data/timeseries-common.csv | csvcut -c fips,date,county,cases,deaths,recovered,positive_tests,negative_tests,total_tests | csvlook |less` but all the FIPS appear to be blank for negative_tests. This PR turns it into something that looks realistic.

48431 is a small county in rural Texas, which had positive_tests from CDS that was 0 for months, went up to 1 and back to 0 and back to 1. This PR changes to Valorum data that looks better.

17031 is Cook County / Chicago. Raised issue in `CAN // Valorum Scraping Tracker` google sheet.

48451 is Tom Green County, TX. Raised issue in `CAN // Valorum Scraping Tracker` google sheet.
Same for 48135 Ector County, TX

Added model output snapsnots

The model in it's current state has been vetted for accuracy. To fully
leverage this moment, I have created a directory of snapshots which
reflect the output of the model.

A test class has been created to compare the output of the model in it's
current configuration to these outputs, so that if the output begins to
change we know about it. Should give us more confidence about the
model's accuracy in the future.

stabilize the inputs as well. That's next

message:
Estimate 1st dose data if it's been missing recently.

Previously we wouldn't estimate 1st dose data from completed if there was any
1st dose data at all.

With this change, we look back 16 days and if there's no 1st dose data in that
span, then we estimate 1st dose from completed. This is necessary since some
of the new CDC timeseries data has stale 1st dose data for some reason and we
want to go ahead and use estimated data up to present so we can show it
on the website.

message:
Dataset class change

way the Datasets retrieve the data to allow for data of an unknown
structure.

The get_'____'_data functions are now expected to be overridden by the
child classes and will perform not only the retrieval but also the
formatting of the incoming data into the expected structure.
