author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Infer RT Improvements - Auto Sigma, Avoid Rounding (#505)

Changes to Rteff inference process that improve accuracy for low counts (changes to the gaussian sigma process, avoiding rounding of smoothed timeseries) and general interpretability of the results (removing deaths and hospitalizations from the composite Rt, increasing the smoothing window width for cases and introducing smoothing to the resulting Rt). The resulting Rt timeseries are much more accurate for low case counts and agree much more closely with leading sites such as rt.live and epiforecasts.io though there are still some differences (see below).

The logic for generating the gaussian process_matrix (which supports Rt changing over time by smoothing the prior distribution each day) is generalized to auto adjust the amount of smoothing depending on the recent (last 10 days or so) scale of counts (width of smoothing window scales with 1/sqrt(counts) to a maximum). This addresses a bias where new likelihood signals from low case counts (which are weaker having a broader distribution) are not able to move a narrow prior distribution causing Rt to significant lag (up to >30 days in some cases) even in the presence of a consistent signal in likelihood. An issue with symmetry of the smoothing window, that was already present but less frequently impactful due to the low value of sigma) was also addressed removing a bias towards Rt values in the middle, Rt = (10 + 0)/2 = 5, of the distribution range. These changes much improve accuracy for lower case counts (<200 impacting about half of all states and most counties) but reduce the amount of “smoothing” in the inference process allowing more existing noise to propagate into the result.

Additionally the process for generating the likelihood signal, which previously needed an integral input, was generalized (using interpolation) to accept float inputs which dramatically improves accuracy of Rt and reduces (shot) noise for very low case counts (<10).

In general the accuracy and consistent interpretability of Rt inference is also greatly impacted by returning a composite result that is the weighted average of Rt determined from timeseries for cases (what is expected) and deaths (generally not done). While there were good motivations for this, side effects include poor interpretability (peaks in new cases no longer align with Rt=1, …), poor consistency (sometimes deaths are not available or have much lower stats). Additionally deaths lag cases by many days so this reduces the usefulness of Rt as a leading indicator. For these reasons the composite Rt was changed to be derived only from cases (though the other contributions are still calculated so they can be used for other purposes).

Finally the smoothing applied to the case timeseries was improved to ensure that the window_size (14) and kernel_width (5) are compatible. The existing code has too narrow a window_size which clipped the gaussian kernel introducing sudden discontinuities in the slope of the smoothed signal. This was greatly reduced by increasing the window_size to 19. Smoothing was also introduced to the final Rt signal which is able to reduce noise (and improve confidence intervals) without introducing further artifacts into the process of the Rt inference process. This smoothing conserves the integral of Rt over time and hence conserves the overall scale change of the underlying case signal.

The end result of all these changes is an Rt signal that is much more accurate for low counts, much more interpretable, and much more consistent with results from other leading sites publishing Rt values. There are still the following issues to address:
1. There are no unit tests that quantitatively compare inferred Rt to what is known to be the correct value (in test data)
2. The case smoothing process is not consistent in time. At the start and end of a timeseries it “slows down” which forces Rt 50% from the true value towards 1
3. The testing volume adjustments made in the code do not seem to be as effective as those made by others (e.g. rt.live)
4. Our logic, based on the Bettencourt approach, is consider “old” now and leading sites are using more general and robust MCMC algorithms. But these are 100s of times slower and will probably never be viable to run at the county level.
5. Rt results are in “reported” time while many other sites show “onset” time so our results lag those by about 7 days. Whether or not to change this is a product question.

author: Brett <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
ICU Estimation from Cumulative ICU Data

Improve the estimation of current icu covid patients in the case where we are only provided with cumulative icu patients.

Sometimes covidtracking provides cumulative, but not current, data for hospitalization and icu. We then estimate the number of patients currently in the ICU. There are multiple things with this implementation that need to be improved, however they can be done in stages. The first stage is to standardize the calculation of ICU. Right now the estimate uses a variable drawn from a wide distribution (roughly 8.6 +/- 2.6 days). This introduces a large source of noise in the snapshot to snapshot calculations. In other places this code is usually called multiple times and then averaged, but for here it is just called once. Instead of bumping up the call/average, I just calculated the value from the means. The consistancy day-to-day is key, especially since this parameter isn't used in any monte-carlo modeling.

I left the hospitilization branch still drawing from the distribution, but averaging over 250 samples. Timeit shows an increase from 8.4ms to 27.2ms. If this becomes significant, we can refactor the params code and surface this constant.

Finally, our new linter just came online, so there will be misc line cleanups for a bit.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
Regional subsets in combined_datasets (#919)

This PR addresses https://trello.com/c/VP9NRpJe/778 and implements pretty close to the notes in https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/wlchtiqvq0cs9aj5lnbfm/Importing-CAN-scraper-data.paper?dl=0&rlkey=zz76hxsiqgg4srkurcutt6pc5

With this change we can add things like `datasource_regions(NYTimesDataset, exclude=ALL_NYC_REGIONS)` or `datasource_regions(CDCTestingDataset, RegionMask(AggregationLevel.COUNTY, states=['TX', 'NY']), exclude=Region.from_fips("06037"))` to the big maps in combined_datasets.py.

* Adds `RegionMask` frozen dataclass, a function to expand it to location_id
* Adds `DataSourceAndRegionMasks`, a DataSource class and include/exclude region masks. Instances of this class can be used in the same places where the DataSource type are used
* Replaces use of the current `NYTimesDataset` class with a new `DataSourceAndRegionMasks` that excludes `ALL_NYC_REGIONS`. Removes the region filter that was in nytimes_dataset.py

## Tested

Ran `./run.py data update`. `dir -lrt data/multiregon*` shows the files were re-written recently and `git status` shows they are not modified from the main branch.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
Use location_id multiregion combined data and add CBSA aggregator (#683)

This PR is part of https://trello.com/c/nYgDEl3M/385-ability-to-query-raw-data-by-msa

* Adds `CountyToCBSAAggregator` and test which is first attempt at aggregating counties to MSAs.
* Removes unused `libs.qa.dataset_summary.get_summaries`
* Adds `xlrd` to requirements.txt
* Changes combined_dataset to be saved as a MultiRegionTimeseriesDataset with location_id instead of TimeseriesDataset with FIPS.
* removes save_summary parameter `--level` because it isn't reason enough to expand the API of MultiRegionTimeseriesDataset 
* Adds dataset_base.SaveableDatasetInterface which sits under DatasetBase in the class hierarchy with stuff it has in common with MultiRegionTimeseriesDataset

## Tested

I ran `python ./run.py data update` and it regenerated an identical data/timeseries.csv. I then skimmed through `vimdiff data/timeseries.csv data/multiregion.csv` to check that the new data file looks the same except for adding a location_id column.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
Add MultiRegionDataset.timeseries_bucketed (#1002)

This PR is part of https://trello.com/c/lvRFxC5y/932-get-dei-vaccination-data-into-api

* Replaces property `MultiRegionDataset.timeseries` with `timeseries_bucketed` that has an index level for the demographic bucket. Access to the old attribute is preserved with a `@cached_property` method.
* Adds a custom `MultiRegionDataset.__init__` that transforms `timeseries` to `timeseries_bucketed` when an object is created. Even calls to `dataclasses.replace` go through this. This constructor raises in the ambiguous case of both parameters being not None.
* Changes existing places that create a `MultiRegionDataset` using `dataclasses.replace` to include `timeseries_bucketed=None` . Subsequent PRs will replace each of these code paths with something that preserves the bucket information.

## Tested

`./run.py data update` produced identical output.

`tests/libs/generate_api_v2_test.py::test_build_summary_for_fips` is known to be failing.

calculate 'effective' r. Doesn't make a huge difference now, but will
make it easier to maintain and update in the future.

message:
fix latest combined column order (#559)

## This PR

* sort columns and rows in LatestValuesDataset before writing
* drop `index` column in LatestValuesDataset
* Dropping rows without FIPS in Timeseries, as produced by JHU but hard to filter in data source class because of the cleanup done in the timeseries class

## Tested

`data/timeseries.csv` is identical.

`git show master:data/latest.csv | git lfs smudge > data/latest-master.csv` and then in jupyter: 
```
import pandas as pd
from covidactnow.datapublic import common_df
from libs.datasets.common_fields import CommonFields

path = 'data/latest-master.csv'
df = common_df.sort_common_field_columns(pd.read_csv(path, dtype={CommonFields.FIPS: str}).set_index(CommonFields.FIPS).sort_index())
df.to_csv(path, date_format="%Y-%m-%d", index=True, float_format="%.12g")
```
and the only difference is the empty index column dropped.

author: Michael Lehenbauer <mikelehen@gmail.com>
message:
Estimate 1st dose data if it's been missing recently.

Previously we wouldn't estimate 1st dose data from completed if there was any
1st dose data at all.

With this change, we look back 16 days and if there's no 1st dose data in that
span, then we estimate 1st dose from completed. This is necessary since some
of the new CDC timeseries data has stale 1st dose data for some reason and we
want to go ahead and use estimated data up to present so we can show it
on the website.

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Refactor Infer_Rt Step 2 (#530)

This PR is the first part of a refactor for our rt inference code.

The infer_rt code now has its own submodule, and has been refactored to accept data agnostic to the aggregation level. This submission does not change any of the major internal components. It just structures the infer_rt code in its own submodule and pulls apart the RtInferenceEngine class into more manageable chunks. Now that Alex's significant improvements have landed, it's time to pay down that technical debt while allowing us to investigate new aggregation levels.

This change is in support of refactoring the inputs into RtInferenceEngine to be agnostic to aggregation level, which will allow for more manageable testing, maintenance, extensibility, and readability. Also, the tests for infer_rt are now under the same file in the test dir.

Outstanding Changes Remaining:
- A change to make the test correction more responsive to data from the last week was removed and will be put as a separate PR.
- Chris made some good recommendations about how to change the internal structure of the code, which will be a separate PR.
- Cli revamps to call a just the infer rt code was separated as a separate PR.
- The whitelist for pyseir and for infer_rt should be completely separated.


* initial commit from stash

* tail suppression addressed, compared with rt.live and inference unit tests working

* generate snapshots for this branch

* fixed breaks caused by merge from master

* first pass at modifying test volume adjustment - not working well yet

* Move infer_rt to Separate Submodule

* ready for Brett made sure all tests working

* Remove Hospitalization Data References from Infer RT

* Remove Cross Dependency on Pyseir Parameter Generation

Note: The serial period is now fixed in InferRtConstants instead of estimated from pyseir. I think it's reasonable to maintain these separately.

* Enforce RtInferenceEngine Accesses InferRtConstants Only Through Init

First step to isolate cross dependencies on the infer_rt script. Most of these should be class variables instead of instance variables, but that's for another time. Right now the goal is to make it clear that everything in the RtInferenceEngine is self contained.

* Extract Plotting Boilerplate to Separate File

* Cleanup for PR Submission

* Update deploy_api.yml

* Fix requirements vs requirements_test error

* Pull Data Loader out of RtInferenceEngine

Make the core Infer Rt Code Agnostic to the Aggregation Level.

* Remove Import Rename in CLI by Renaming Fun

As per PR#530, we are simplifying the Bettencourt Rt inference work. Part of that work was making a separate submodule. The cli api was inconsistent about calling this method (all the other ones prepend run_). This change fixes that inconsistency. It will break old api calls that directly called infer_rt (instead of run_infer_rt). The cli is almost exclusively used internally, so I think this change is worth the possible confusion, especially because it will fail loudly and quickly.

* Apply Filtering at the Data Loading Step

* Refactor Tests to Take Advantage of New Infer Rt Signature

The infer rt tests now use the new method of passing in a dataframe. All tests pass, but I think that's more a function of bad test coverage. Especially around initialization. A good opportunity to create more tests!

* Infer Rt Tests

* rt inference tests running, figure_collector implemented and used by tests, charting of smoothed cases included again

* Adding test_results directory + a bit of test cleanup

* Removing Merge df Code to be Added as a Separate Branch

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
add _apply_scaling_factor and test (#813)

This PR builds on https://github.com/covid-projections/covid-data-model/pull/811 to add scaling of certain timeseries using certain static values.

Not hard-coding the fields may be making this code more flexible than we need, but does make writing small unit tests easier.

This development direction uses panda parallel operations pretty heavily to get the speed to aggregate all CBSA's in a few seconds on my laptop. This makes the code somewhat harder to read because each value and operation must handle multiple locations at the same time. For example, instead of multiplying by a scalar weight the code needs to multiple by a vector of weights indexed by location.

Alternative development directions that have code paths processing one location at a time are likely easier to read but harder to run. Panda's builtin aggregation functions are not flexible enough to do things like weighted averages. It'd be really nice to have a function that takes the unaggregated static + timeseries DataFrame for each aggregated region, and returns the static and timeseries of that one region. A simple test with `apply` suggests this will take ~30min to run with bare python. It is quite possible numba can bring that down to a few seconds, but I haven't tried. It'd be nice if we had an easy way to run this in the cloud (I'd like to try Dask/Prefect) but that is a much bigger task.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
Move annotations into MultiRegionDataset.tag (#877)

## This PR

This PR is part of https://trello.com/c/Cq2zNk2M/674-annotate-data-outliers-that-weve-flagged-in-the-ui

With this change annotations get all the way from the tail filter to the final combined data object. Next step will be writing and reading them and getting them to the API code.

* Adds method `MulitRegionDataset.append_tag_df`. 
* Tweaks `MulitRegionDataset.__post_init__` to explicitly check for dates instead of depending on `to_datetime` raising an exception. This catches places where a string representation of date gets into the index.
* Moves access to annotations from through `TailFilter.annotations_as_dataframe()` to `MulitRegionDataset.annotations_as_dataframe()`. 
* Adds test_helper code for tags/annotations

## Tested

Ran the following commands to check that annotations made their way to the final MulitRegionDataset.  The `csvcut` is there to make the column order consistent with the current output. The only diff is annotations for us-vi metrics were dropped because we don't have population data for VI.
```
./run.py data update
cp data/multiregion-annotations.csv data/multiregion-annotations.csv-as-written
csvcut -c location_id,variable,tag_type,content,date data/multiregion-annotations.csv-as-written > data/multiregion-annotations.csv
git difftool --no-prompt -t vimdiff main -- data/multiregion-annotations.csv
```

python ./run.py utils save-combined-latest-csv --output-dir output/

python ./run.py utils save-combined-csv --output-dir output/
python ./run.py utils save-combined-latest-csv --output-dir output/

message:
Add tag and annotation to OneRegionTimeseriesDataset (#881)

This PR is part of https://trello.com/c/Cq2zNk2M/674-annotate-data-outliers-that-weve-flagged-in-the-ui

* Copies all tags associated with a location_id to `OneRegionTimeseriesDataset` when creating it
* Makes `OneRegionTimeseriesDataset.provenance` from the tag DataFrame
* Adds `TagInTimeseries`, a frozen dataclass to represent a tag in the context of a particular timeseries. Use it in production code to iterate through tags and to replace named tuple `AnnotationInTimeseriesLiteral`. Unfortunately it is harder to make a literal dataclass than a tuple so adds `make_tag` to simplify making them in tests.
* Extracts code that turns a list of tags to a DataFrame to `make_tag_df` where it can be reused by a test calling `append_tag_df`

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Apply Shim Method Consistently Across Total_Hospitalized, ICU, and Deaths (#506)

This PR addresses issue https://trello.com/c/aXp44GbY/233-fix-projection-scaling.

The method that was applied to cumulative deaths is extended to also apply to ICU and Total Hospitalized.

The most important changes to note are the following:
- Shim to Direct County Provided Values: For both ICU and Total Hospitalization we will now directly shim to provided county data where available. In the past, county results were only scaled on the ratio between pyseir state and pyseir model county ratios.
-  Stricter Shimming Across Aggregation Levels: We are pushing to collect as much county specific data as possible. In the meantime, we will no longer scale county level PySEIR outputs based on the higher aggregate level. If we aren't comfortable giving a prediction for a high granularity region, then we shouldn't provide results (or in the future make it clearer that we are doing a weighted distribution of the state's values. If a county does not having any hospitalization data, then we serve the model outputs. This will clarify the need for better data coverage and better estimates in low data coverage zones.
- Linear Shim instead of Multiplicative Shim for ICU headroom and hospitalizations. Forecasts were unacceptably sensitive to the multiplication shim (since it was being broadcast 1-3 months in the future). The day to day stability of the outputs was insufficient. The goal of correcting to current value was still required, and the decision was made to apply a linear shim instead. This has the artifact that the initial condition need not be zero (y may not equal 0 at x=0), but it was decided that this was the lesser of two evils for right now.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
backfill_vaccination_initiated incorrectly added empty time series (#1096)

This PR fixes a bug in `backfill_vaccination_initiated` that I noticed while working on https://github.com/covid-projections/covid-data-model/pull/1094

`computed_initiated` was being kept even when it was all NA for a location+bucket. This happens when one or both of administered and completed were all NA. The bug cause combined datasets to include a row with a derived tag but no real values. The fix is changing dropna axis param to `0, or ‘index’ : Drop rows which contain missing values.` (from DataFrame.dropna docs).

## Tested

```
./run.py data update
git difftool --no-prompt -t vimdiff main -- data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv
```
shows 2533 dropped empty `vaccinations_initiated` for various buckets that all have derived tag `{}`.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
API with source and source_url combined (#944)

This PR is part of https://trello.com/c/lbiZpKwH/849-proposal-improve-the-provenance-link-so-that-we-can-show-a-source-urls-instead-of-a-data-class

* Changes API output to merge source and source_url. `source` is now an object instead of a string taken from an enum.

before
```
{
  "sources": ["CANScrapersStateProviders"], 
  "anomalies": [],
  "source_url": "https://www.dshs.state.tx.us/coronavirus/immunize/vaccine.aspx"
}
```

after
```
{
  "sources": [{
    "type": "CANScrapersStateProviders",
    "url": "https://www.dshs.state.tx.us/coronavirus/immunize/vaccine.aspx",
    "name": null
  }], 
  "anomalies": []
}
```

## Tested

Looked at 
```
python pyseir/cli.py build-all --generate-api-v2 -s TX --fips 48507
jq .  < output/county/48507.timeseries.json | less
```

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Apply Shim to Cumulative Death s.t. Latest Observed Equals Latest Model (#502)

Our model tracks incident deaths. We present a cumulative deaths value in the FE in the table for different forecasted observations.

The model can accumulate tracking error for the cumulative deaths. In some cases this is significant enough to raise questions in the "estimated cumulative deaths". We are actively re-evaluating the forecasts and table, but for now, we apply a shim to correct for this tracking error. This will take the cumulative deaths timeseries and apply a constant value to shift the graph s.t. today's model value matches with today's observed.

https://trello.com/c/ZDNt3or6/247-shim-model-cumulative-deaths-to-observed

* Apply Shim to Cumulative Death s.t. Latest Observed Equals Latest Model

This code shims the cumulative deaths timeseries in the API so that the cumulative deaths from the model agrees with the cumulative deaths from outside observed sources.

message:
Make recent_days configurable per Method, rm positivity calculations from top_level_metrics (#868)

## This PR

* Removes last of test positivity calculations from top_level_metrics, moving function `calculate_test_positivity` from top_level_metrics to test_positivity.
* Adds a new `test_positivity.Method` called `OldMethod` that reproduces what was done in top_level_metrics
* Makes recent_days configurable per Method because OldMethod used 10 days instead of 14
* Changes `test_positivity.Method.calculate` to return an `MethodOutput` object holding all timeseries for debugging and only recent timeseries as the desired output
* Changes `test_positivity.Method.name` from str to DatasetName because each method is used to produce one dataset
* Adds support for copying provenance from the input dataset to the output dataset in test_positivity
* Adds ugly hack/workaround so recent_days can have a default value in a super class.
* Hacks in OldMethodAll as a fall back when everything else is expired
* Moves `test_top_level_metrics_recent_pos_neg_tests_has_positivity_ratio` to `test_recent_pos_neg_tests_has_positivity_ratio` and use `read_csv...skipinitialspace=True` to make csv easier to read

## Tested

Ran `python ./run.py api generate-test-positivity` and found output identical to master *except* has some regions where the old method produces a timeseries that is all NA but considered valid and recent because the input timeseries is recent. Applying a fix to master in branch `tgb-positivity-old-calc-no-empty` got the same output.

I compared the API output for the state of NY in master and the branch using command such as `python ./run.py api generate-api-v2 -o output/output-ny-positivity-calc-in-methods --state NY output/output-ny-positivity-calc-in-methods` and the diffs looked insignificant.

Refactored the python script written by David Strauss into a Jupyter
notebook. Also made an effort to change the script to be easier to
maintain and to read:

  functions.

main goal was to put a framework around the model that would make it
easier to maintain and fix in the future by isolating logic wherever possible.

of the original model to python by David S, and then to Jupyter by me,

message:
Pickle MultiRegionDataset (#1111)

Add simple support for serialization and deserialization of `MultiRegionDataset` using python pickle. Files created like this are much smaller than any CSV (less than 1/2 a wide-dates file). Compared to parquet and hd5 this makes restoring the entire object trivial but the files are not easy to read outside of Python.

Adds the raw combined data to the data dashboard.

Adds a command to copy a pickle file to CSV. For example: `./run.py data pickle-to-csv data/multiregion.pkl.gz data/multiregion.pkl-wide-dates.csv`

To dump a time series from the new combined raw file try:

```
from libs.datasets.timeseries import MultiRegionDataset
import pathlib

ds = MultiRegionDataset.from_compressed_pickle(pathlib.Path('data/combined-raw.pkl.gz'))
ds.timeseries_bucketed_wide_dates.loc[('iso1:us', 'cases', 'all'), :]
```

message:
Refactor drop_observations (#1085)

This PR is part of https://trello.com/c/f27O08ea/1266-make-it-possible-to-block-in-the-backend-using-the-cms

Most of these changes are done to simplify drop_observations because https://github.com/covid-projections/covid-data-model/pull/1080 uses different subsets of the code.

* changes manual_filter config to use a pydantic model instead of unstructured JSON
* replaces MultiRegionDataset.remove_regions with MultiRegionDataset.partition_by_region
* adds MultiRegionDataset.replace_timeseries_wide_dates which is used in the new manual filter code and replaces some funky use of dataclasses.replace in ca_vaccination_backfill.py
* adds RegionMask comments
* changes KnownIssue.date to a datetime instead of panda timestamp, for better compatibility with pydantic

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Apply Shim Method Consistently Across Total_Hospitalized, ICU, and Deaths (#506)

This PR addresses issue https://trello.com/c/aXp44GbY/233-fix-projection-scaling.

The method that was applied to cumulative deaths is extended to also apply to ICU and Total Hospitalized.

The most important changes to note are the following:
- Shim to Direct County Provided Values: For both ICU and Total Hospitalization we will now directly shim to provided county data where available. In the past, county results were only scaled on the ratio between pyseir state and pyseir model county ratios.
-  Stricter Shimming Across Aggregation Levels: We are pushing to collect as much county specific data as possible. In the meantime, we will no longer scale county level PySEIR outputs based on the higher aggregate level. If we aren't comfortable giving a prediction for a high granularity region, then we shouldn't provide results (or in the future make it clearer that we are doing a weighted distribution of the state's values. If a county does not having any hospitalization data, then we serve the model outputs. This will clarify the need for better data coverage and better estimates in low data coverage zones.
- Linear Shim instead of Multiplicative Shim for ICU headroom and hospitalizations. Forecasts were unacceptably sensitive to the multiplication shim (since it was being broadcast 1-3 months in the future). The day to day stability of the outputs was insufficient. The goal of correcting to current value was still required, and the decision was made to apply a linear shim instead. This has the artifact that the initial condition need not be zero (y may not equal 0 at x=0), but it was decided that this was the lesser of two evils for right now.

message:
Refactored script into jupyter notebook

Refactored the python script written by David Strauss into a Jupyter
notebook. Also made an effort to change the script to be easier to
maintain and to read:
- Reafactored the calculations for all of the variables into their own
  functions.
- Refactored the iterative loop into it's own function.
- Streamlined the creation of the DataFrame product.

It's not perfect, and I probably made a few mistakes along the way. My
main goal was to put a framework around the model that would make it
easier to maintain and fix in the future by isolating logic wherever possible.

The products of this model will need to be vigorously vetted to ensure
that they are correct. It is highly likely that during the translation
of the original model to python by David S, and then to Jupyter by me,
a mistake was made and the model broken.

message:
Share loaded data sources between latest and timeseries combined data (#609)

## This PR

* Moves code that changes a `DataSource` into a `DatasetBase` from combined_datasets, latest_values_dataset.py, timeseries.py to data_source.py.
* Load data sources before calling _build_combined_dataset_from_sources so that the loaded values can be used in multiple calls. Because `DataSource.latest` sometimes calls `DataSource.timeseries` the cache saves a bunch of processing time, reducing time as measured by `/usr/bin/time -v ./run.py data update` from 6 to 5 minutes.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
Run each county in a process (#652)

This PR is part of https://trello.com/c/nYgDEl3M/385-ability-to-query-raw-data-by-msa

This PR
* factors out a new abstraction: `StatePipeline` and `SubStateRegionPipeline`. They are responsible for running the pipelines and storing the outputs. This is motivated by the need to have the old `_state_only_pipeline` return model_fitter and infer_rt data. It this point we don't need a common subclass so I haven't made one.
* changes how counties (aka sub-state regions) are run. Instead of each stage being run in parallel across all regions, then the next stage, now all counties are run in parallel down the entire pipeline. Hopefully this will be faster due to less data copying and less blocking.
* removes duplicate infer_rt of states, called out by Brett's "Note: double calculates the state fips"
* removes more intermediate files
* extract SubStateRegionPipelineInput construction to a static build_all method
* change ensemble_runner.RegionalInput to get state data as a parameter instead of from disk and remove from_fips which no longer works for substate/county regions
* rm model_fitter.run_counties_of_state that wasn't used in the main pipeline run.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
read and transform parquet file during data update (#934)

This PR will help with https://trello.com/c/lbiZpKwH/849-proposal-improve-the-provenance-link-so-that-we-can-show-a-source-urls-instead-of-a-data-class because it lets us skip adding source_url in covid-data-public CSVs. It also simplifies the process of adding new fields in general to combined_datasets.

* Adds a new (and hacky) `CanScraperBase` that caches the CAN parquet file after it has been loaded
* Changes `CANScraperStateProviders`, `CDCTestingDataset` and `CDCVaccinesDataset` to depend on their scripts in the covid-data-public repo. After the scripts are turned off we can move the source to this repo
* Adds a pip dependency on python-snappy to fix  ..../fastparquet/compression.py line 144, in decompress_data RuntimeError: Decompression 'SNAPPY' not available. 

## Tested

In `main` ran `time ./run.py data update` and got
```
real	14m53.280s
user	10m39.442s
sys	3m46.207s
```

then checked out this branch, ran the same and got
```
real	9m43.823s
user	7m48.892s
sys	1m39.757s
```

with the same output in `data` except for the covid-data-model repo state.

message:
add ensemble_runner.RegionalInput.from_model_fitter and use it for counties (#639)

This PR is part of https://trello.com/c/nYgDEl3M/385-ability-to-query-raw-data-by-msa

* In `ensemble_runner` and `webui_data_adaptor_v1` add constructor `Regionalnput.from_model_fitter` which copies data directly from a `ModelFitter` object, saving a round trip to disk.
* Remove `webui_data_adaptor_v1` `generate_state` which was only used for regions in one place.
* Remove `if __main__` in `webui_data_adaptor_v1` that looked like some kind of early test
* Remove `model_fitter.RegionalInput.load_inference_result` which wasn't used from other classes
* Remove `execute_model_for_fips` which added a branch that always went one way
* Move the `states_only=False` part of `model_fitter.run_state` to it's own function because it had a single caller and complicated using `Regionalnput.from_model_fitter`
* Adds use of a tempdir to `test_pyseir_end_to_end_idaho` so it doesn't pass when output from a previous run is still in `output/`
* Removes first of two writes of state data, at the end of `_state_only_pipeline` and inline the remaining caller of `cli._map_outputs`

message:
add support for reading and writing with bucket. (#1021)

This PR is part of https://trello.com/c/lvRFxC5y/932-get-dei-vaccination-data-into-api.

* Changes `timeseries_bucketed_wide_dates` to return bucket as inner/right index level to be more consistent with idea that a set of time-series form a distribution within one metric/variable.
* Changes `read_from_pointer` to load the bucket if the column is present and assume `all` if not
* Changes `timeseries_rows` (which is called by `write_to_dataset_pointer`) to include bucket in the index

## Tested

`./run.py data update` adds demographic_bucket column always containing "all". 

Confirmed that nothing else changed with
```
mv data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv data/multiregion-wide-dates-demo.csv
csvcut -C demographic_bucket data/multiregion-wide-dates-demo.csv | perl -np -e 's/,+$//' > data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv
git status
```

message:
Fixed the missing backfill dates problem

Swapped the order of the cutoff and the backfill functions in the data
prep step.

The problem was being caused by holes in the data. If there is data on
feb 1, but nothing else until mar 10, then the backfill function will do
nothing because there's data prior to the cutoff date, then the cutoff
function will remove the feb data and the first date left will be the
10th. Now we cutoff first and backfill second.

message:
Adding disclaimer to some Texas counties

* depends on https://github.com/covid-projections/covid-data-public/pull/145

## Tested

message:
Simplify ICU Utilization Numerator Estimate (#623)

Use a Linear Regression and Case-Based State-to-County disaggregation to estimate the ICU Utilization numerator (number of COVID related heads in ICU beds).

We estimate the current icu by the following order:

1. Take current icu if available
2. Take current hospitalization if available for that level and convert (via simple pre-trained Linear Regression) to current icu.
3. Take current icu of the higher aggregate (state) if available and disaggregate based on the normalized case load of that county vs. state for the past month (pre-computed).
4. Take current hospitalized for the higher aggregate (state), which is always available, and disaggregate as above.

This model involves two pre-computed models:

1. The linear regression from current hospitalized to current icu.
2. The weights from state to county.
3. These will be planned to be updated out-of-loop approx twice a month.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
combined_datasets with dataset objects (#914)

## This PR

This is inspired by brainstorms in https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/wlchtiqvq0cs9aj5lnbfm/Importing-CAN-scraper-data.paper . It doesn't add a new representation for creating subsets of DataSource objects per region but does let us re-use the existing `get_subset` to add subsets to the per-field lists in combined_datasets.

* changes `timeseries.combined_datasets` to take map with dataset values instead of names. this makes it easier to inject data with different region subsets
* adds a bunch of caching to replace the reuse of values that happened when they were referred to by names

## Tested

Ran `./run.py data update`. `dir -lrt data/multiregon*` shows the files were re-written recently and `git status` shows they are not modified from the main branch.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
MultiRegionDataset.geo_data (#1011)

This PR addresses https://trello.com/c/cmh0RhsA/1071-remove-geo-data-from-multiregiondatasetsstatic

A MultiRegionDataset needs level,state (aka geo data columns) etc for making subsets of it to work consistently. Before this change subset may or may not work depending on how the MultiRegionDataset was created. This PR fixes that be making sure every MultiRegionDataset has geo data.

* Adds `data/geo-data.csv`, a location_id indexed table of values (FIPS, county name, state, country, level) that we can maintain manually because they are even more static than the scalars in `ALL_FIELDS_FEATURE_DEFINITION`.
* Drops geo data columns when creating a MultiRegionDataset, warning when values conflict with geo-data.csv.
* Adds geo_data property that dynamically makes a table of the geo-data for location in the dataset when needed
* Moves most of the logic for interpreting RegionMaskOrRegion from combined_datasets to timeseries now that the later has consistent access to geo data.
* Fixes a bunch of tests that had bogus FIPS and location_id

## Tested

`./run.py data update` then 
`git cat-file blob main:data/multiregion-static.csv| git lfs smudge | csvcut -C fips,state,country,county,aggregate_level > data/multiregion-static-main.csv` to get the existing data without columns expected to be removed.
`diff data/multiregion-static.csv data/multiregion-static-main.csv` shows no diff and `git status` lists only the expected json and static data changes.

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Infer RT Improvements - Auto Sigma, Avoid Rounding (#505)

Changes to Rteff inference process that improve accuracy for low counts (changes to the gaussian sigma process, avoiding rounding of smoothed timeseries) and general interpretability of the results (removing deaths and hospitalizations from the composite Rt, increasing the smoothing window width for cases and introducing smoothing to the resulting Rt). The resulting Rt timeseries are much more accurate for low case counts and agree much more closely with leading sites such as rt.live and epiforecasts.io though there are still some differences (see below).

The logic for generating the gaussian process_matrix (which supports Rt changing over time by smoothing the prior distribution each day) is generalized to auto adjust the amount of smoothing depending on the recent (last 10 days or so) scale of counts (width of smoothing window scales with 1/sqrt(counts) to a maximum). This addresses a bias where new likelihood signals from low case counts (which are weaker having a broader distribution) are not able to move a narrow prior distribution causing Rt to significant lag (up to >30 days in some cases) even in the presence of a consistent signal in likelihood. An issue with symmetry of the smoothing window, that was already present but less frequently impactful due to the low value of sigma) was also addressed removing a bias towards Rt values in the middle, Rt = (10 + 0)/2 = 5, of the distribution range. These changes much improve accuracy for lower case counts (<200 impacting about half of all states and most counties) but reduce the amount of “smoothing” in the inference process allowing more existing noise to propagate into the result.

Additionally the process for generating the likelihood signal, which previously needed an integral input, was generalized (using interpolation) to accept float inputs which dramatically improves accuracy of Rt and reduces (shot) noise for very low case counts (<10).

In general the accuracy and consistent interpretability of Rt inference is also greatly impacted by returning a composite result that is the weighted average of Rt determined from timeseries for cases (what is expected) and deaths (generally not done). While there were good motivations for this, side effects include poor interpretability (peaks in new cases no longer align with Rt=1, …), poor consistency (sometimes deaths are not available or have much lower stats). Additionally deaths lag cases by many days so this reduces the usefulness of Rt as a leading indicator. For these reasons the composite Rt was changed to be derived only from cases (though the other contributions are still calculated so they can be used for other purposes).

Finally the smoothing applied to the case timeseries was improved to ensure that the window_size (14) and kernel_width (5) are compatible. The existing code has too narrow a window_size which clipped the gaussian kernel introducing sudden discontinuities in the slope of the smoothed signal. This was greatly reduced by increasing the window_size to 19. Smoothing was also introduced to the final Rt signal which is able to reduce noise (and improve confidence intervals) without introducing further artifacts into the process of the Rt inference process. This smoothing conserves the integral of Rt over time and hence conserves the overall scale change of the underlying case signal.

The end result of all these changes is an Rt signal that is much more accurate for low counts, much more interpretable, and much more consistent with results from other leading sites publishing Rt values. There are still the following issues to address:
1. There are no unit tests that quantitatively compare inferred Rt to what is known to be the correct value (in test data)
2. The case smoothing process is not consistent in time. At the start and end of a timeseries it “slows down” which forces Rt 50% from the true value towards 1
3. The testing volume adjustments made in the code do not seem to be as effective as those made by others (e.g. rt.live)
4. Our logic, based on the Bettencourt approach, is consider “old” now and leading sites are using more general and robust MCMC algorithms. But these are 100s of times slower and will probably never be viable to run at the county level.
5. Rt results are in “reported” time while many other sites show “onset” time so our results lag those by about 7 days. Whether or not to change this is a product question.

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Fix ICU Utilization Metric When Incorporating New 'Cumulative ICU' Datastream (#427)

Updated the 'estimate current number of hospital/icu beds occupied' by improving the model initialization and removing some unplanned sources of variability.

* ICU Estimation from Cumulative ICU Data

Improve the estimation of current icu covid patients in the case where we are only provided with cumulative icu patients.

Sometimes covidtracking provides cumulative, but not current, data for hospitalization and icu. We then estimate the number of patients currently in the ICU. There are multiple things with this implementation that need to be improved, however they can be done in stages. The first stage is to standardize the calculation of ICU. Right now the estimate uses a variable drawn from a wide distribution (roughly 8.6 +/- 2.6 days). This introduces a large source of noise in the snapshot to snapshot calculations. In other places this code is usually called multiple times and then averaged, but for here it is just called once. Instead of bumping up the call/average, I just calculated the value from the means. The consistancy day-to-day is key, especially since this parameter isn't used in any monte-carlo modeling.

I left the hospitilization branch still drawing from the distribution, but averaging over 250 samples. Timeit shows an increase from 8.4ms to 27.2ms. If this becomes significant, we can refactor the params code and surface this constant.

Finally, our new linter just came online, so there will be misc line cleanups for a bit.

* Parameter Scope Reduction for Temporary Test

The added parameter tripped up code elsewhere that has a script list of allowed keys. This constant is now local, but will be incorporated into the params later.

* Refactoring Current_To_Cumulative Code

Trying to isolate the code that converts current to cumulative from the code that just loads any data.

* Refactored Current to Cumulative Outside Load Data

Extracted the logic to convert cumulative totals to an estimate of current patient population. Before this, it was added into a data loading function as an optional flag. That structure was too constraining to include required features of the model (i.e. requiring more than one value provided to extrapolate from).

* Documentation and Reformatting

Combined DataSources using MultiRegionDataset, remove latest values (#829)

## This PR

* Deletes most of `LatestValuesDataset` and `TimeseriesDataset`
* Deletes `combined_datasets.build_from_sources`, the old dataset merger.
* Moves aggregations that were in `LatestValuesDataset` to aggregate_puerto_rico_from_counties and aggregate_to_new_york_city.
* Fixes NYC test positivity aggregation by using timeseries.aggregate_regions
* Updates `libs/qa/common_df_diff.py` to use location_id instead of fips
* Makes crude attempt at fixing `libs/qa/data_availability.py` to use static_and_timeseries_latest_with_fips() without LatestValuesDataset. Tests pass but otherwise not tested.

## Tested

Ran `./run.py data update` (which finishes in about 1-2min on my laptop, vs 5-6 mins before this change).
The only change in `git difftool -t vimdiff master -- data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv` is NYC test_positivity looks much better and NYC lost provenance information because it isn't passed on in aggregation. `data/multiregion-static.csv` is unchanged from master.

message:
Use unaggregated country data (#1100)

This PR addresses https://trello.com/c/sJDKzKIU/1302-make-usa-aggregation-use-incoming-usa-data-if-it-exists-rather-than-aggregate-the-states

* Factored out aggregation to the US country region so it is easy to add a unit test.
* Adds US population count in data source `fips_population.py` so that us country data isn't dropped by `drop_regions_without_population`.
* Adds property `MultiRegionDataset.variables` giving easy access to all variables in the dataset index
* Adds `MultiRegionDataset.drop_na_columns` which drops variables that don't have any real values

### Tested

`./run.py data update` and `git difftool --no-prompt -t vimdiff main -- data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv` shows only cases, deaths, new_cases and new_deaths change. They now include the NYT source tag and the values changed a tiny bit.

author: Michael Lehenbauer <michael@covidactnow.org>
message:
Remove ICU headroom and typical usage rate from API. (#1177)

This is a big cleanup change (to delete deprecated code) with some resulting API changes:
* `icuHeadroomRatio` (as a metric value and as a metric risk level [low, medium, high, etc.]), `icuHeadroomDetails`, and `typicalUsageRate` are removed from the API. We announced that we were planning to delete these APIs several months ago (and have not been maintaining them) but hadn't gotten around to deleting them.
* `hospitalBeds.capacity` now uses our STAFFED_BEDS column (from the HHS hospital dataset) instead of MAX_BED_COUNT (from the [CovidCareMap](https://www.covidcaremap.org/) dataset that we were never very happy with). This does change the numbers in the API, but it makes `hospitalBeds.capacity` consistent with `icuBeds.capacity` which was already using data from the HHS hospital dataset.  FWIW- We don't use `hospitalBeds.capacity` on the website and I'm not aware of any specific API customers using them.

NOTES:
* With these changes made I was able to delete `CovidCareMapBeds` dataset. 🎉 
* To avoid breaking consumers of our CSV files relying on column ordering, I've replaced the removed columns with "unused" columns.

Note for posterity (from Brett): We originally used Covid Care Map as a static source of 2019 bed capacities. Dave Luo was very helpful.

However, they started updating their data by mixing in updated values as they found them through state resources and news articles. This hybrid datasource was not viable for us since we made some corrections and estimates with the assumption that these were 2019 numbers, not nowcasting numbers.

message:
Added new NowcastingSEIRModel and supporting tests, enabled incremental run on old model (#674)

The first steps towards incorporating a stage-less SEIR model into scenario planning and projections.

The default is to still run the current 3 stage pyseir model. The intention is to split this PR into multiple blocks, with (1) adding the new code and tests the first block, and (2) then using that code to prototype scenario planners, and (3) having the default values from the new model show up in the API. Right now this is just part 1, which could still theoretically live in a separate branch, but it's been separate long enough that I think it's worth getting it into the modeling, even though it's not running during build-all right now.

* initial commit with steady state ratio determination working on main model and new model running and starting to test against recent FL peak. Still missing demographics, delay turned off and predicted deaths high by a factor of 3.

* decent first pass to matching FL peak behaviour

* applying initial hospitalizations and deaths, added historical data and set of tests for each state

* refactored testing and separated out nowcast model into separate file

* cleaned up some test cases

* updated median and f_d/f_h data and made t_h vary with median_age improving historical fits over 60-90 days

* updated test for iowa projection and SMAPE error measurement of historical tests

* added manual corrections for new deaths for worst spikes and optimized some parameters to get lowest average SMAPE for recent tests (average SMAPE now about .33)

* reorganized code a bit and cleaned up tests

* improved test_run_model_incrementally

* now have test_model_run_incrementally running into the actual future showing how this will work better

* more interesting values in test

* spline(log) generation of r(t) from point case forecasts fit data much better, unit test using Reich Lab new case forecasts to predict new death forecasts

* fixed Natasha defect where t_h variation with age was broken

* added flags to turn off plots in all nowcast tests, too aggressive should refine later. Allows tests to run much faster

* cleaned up some imports and separated some code better

* cleaned up todos, updates some tests

* fixed a bunch of pandas, linting and fig closing warnings

* added create of test_results dir if not present

* one more time fixing path and mkdir

* Adding output dir for test results

* removed nested directories and applied Chris' fix to both tests

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
add pyseir build-all --generate-api-v2 (#843)

## This PR

* Adds `pyseir build-all --generate-api-v2` so making API output is one command after updating combined datasets. This makes testing the API output of newly aggregated and dis-aggregated regions easier.
* Adds `pyseir.run.PyseirOutputDatasets` which wraps reading and writing pyseir output
* Factors out most of click.command generate_api_v2 into generate_api_v2_from_loaded_data which gets data as args instead of from the file system
* Changes pyseir build-all --states-only to --level=state. This adds support for --level=country
* Renames `pyseir.cli.RegionPipeline` to `pyseir.run.OneRegionPipeline`
* Removes `RegionPipelineInput` which wasn't doing much after the fips/states/level filter params were replaced with a combined MultiRegionDataset.

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
GitHub Self-Hosted Runner Queue (#514)

Ensure a Snapshot is Sent to the Github Action Runner as a Single Unit of Work

Enforce a queue to the GitHub self-hosted runner that treats the creation of the entire snapshot as the job.

The previous version separated the workflow into multiple "jobs" that were linearly dependent on each other. That "jobs" abstraction is built to allow parallel processes, and if we used the GitHub hosted version it would run up to 20 jobs in parallel. However, the runner built for self-hosting prioritizes the jobs across snapshots in a way that delays the time to first snapshot completion (without changing the time to last snapshot completion). Instead of completing all the jobs of the first snapshot, it will cycle through each outstanding snapshot request calling the next available job for that snapshot.

It is better to have the early snapshot complete and unblock the person waiting for it.

This is solved by switching a given snapshot to a single job with multiple steps. The "steps" abstraction is the correct mental model that enforces sequential ordering (which we want anyways in our current implementations). So this will send all the commands to the runner as one packet.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
Add USAFacts to get NYC boroughs cases+deaths. Aggregate to new "place" region (#839)

## This PR

* adds USAFacts as backup data source of cases and deaths
* Adds new AggregateLevel PLACE
* Changes NYC aggregation from boroughs to produce data with FIPS 3651000 and location id `iso1:us#iso2:us-ny#fips:3651000`
* Drops NY City data from NYTimes data source so NY County data from USAFacts appears in combined datasets
* Updates combined data to add the county boroughs and place NYC with `./run.py data update`
* Updates weights to add the county boroughs and place NYC with `./run.py data update-case-based-icu-utilization-weights`
* In calls to `get_icu_timeseries_from_regional_input` remove default args that were never used, making the source code closer to what is run

## Tested

Ran `./run.py data update` then `git difftool -t vimdiff master -- data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv` which shows 
* case/deaths/new_cases appearing for some tiny counties (iso1:us#iso2:us-ak#fips:02105, iso1:us#iso2:us-ak#fips:02282, iso1:us#iso2:us-hi#fips:15005
* The boroughs appear with a few stats:
```
iso1:us#iso2:us-ny#fips:36005,cases,USAFacts,,,,,,,,,,,,
iso1:us#iso2:us-ny#fips:36005,deaths,USAFacts,,,,,,,,,,,
iso1:us#iso2:us-ny#fips:36005,negative_tests,Valorum,,,,
iso1:us#iso2:us-ny#fips:36005,new_cases,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,
iso1:us#iso2:us-ny#fips:36005,positive_tests,Valorum,,,,
iso1:us#iso2:us-ny#fips:36005,test_positivity,CMSTesting
```
* FIPS 36061  is replaced with NY County data, looking like the above.
* Changes in `data/multiregion-static.csv` look similar
* `iso1:us#cbsa:35620` appeared. This is `New York-Northern New Jersey-Long Island, NY-NJ-PA` and likely didn't appear before because counties in it were entirely missing

https://github.com/covid-projections/covid-data-model/actions/runs/409039004 built snapshot 1409 from this branch.

Check for ICU headroom stats in the API output by running  `python ./pyseir/cli.py build-all --states NY --generate-api-v2 --output-dir output-tgb-pyseir-no-ny-agg` then looking at `jq .metrics.icuHeadroomRatio output-tgb-pyseir-no-ny-agg/county/36005.json`

Checked the place NYC is output by running `python ./pyseir/cli.py build-all --location-id-matches='.+\#fips\:(36061|3651000|36047|36081|36005|36085)' --generate-api-v2 --output-dir output-nyc` than looking at `output-nyc/place/3651000.json`.

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Apply Shim to Cumulative Death s.t. Latest Observed Equals Latest Model (#502)

Our model tracks incident deaths. We present a cumulative deaths value in the FE in the table for different forecasted observations.

The model can accumulate tracking error for the cumulative deaths. In some cases this is significant enough to raise questions in the "estimated cumulative deaths". We are actively re-evaluating the forecasts and table, but for now, we apply a shim to correct for this tracking error. This will take the cumulative deaths timeseries and apply a constant value to shift the graph s.t. today's model value matches with today's observed.

https://trello.com/c/ZDNt3or6/247-shim-model-cumulative-deaths-to-observed

* Apply Shim to Cumulative Death s.t. Latest Observed Equals Latest Model

This code shims the cumulative deaths timeseries in the API so that the cumulative deaths from the model agrees with the cumulative deaths from outside observed sources.

* Updated as per PR Feedback

* Remove Trigger

* Change `MultiRegionTimeseriesDataset` static method constructors to form a DAG from csv -> combined df, combined df -> ts + latest df, ts + latest objects -> ts + latest df.
* Changes `MultiRegionTimeseriesDataset` and `multiregion.csv` to include the latest/non-timeseries data. This trickles through to `OneRegionTimeseriesDataset` also having latest data and less use of `LatestValuesDataset`.
* Adds `data update --aggregate-to-msa` that calls `statistical_areas.CountyToCBSAAggregator`
* Updates multiregion data, needed to add latest data to the csv, which is needed to get tests passing

Estimate 1st dose data if it's been missing recently. (#1155)

Previously we wouldn't estimate 1st dose data from completed if there was any
1st dose data at all.

With this change, we look back 16 days and if there's no 1st dose data in that
span, then we estimate 1st dose from completed. This is necessary since some
of the new CDC timeseries data has stale 1st dose data for some reason and we
want to go ahead and use estimated data up to present so we can show it
on the website.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
Drop stalled timeseries tails (#855)

## This PR

This PR addresses https://trello.com/c/UKy1yEtd/664-hhs-test-positivity-handle-bad-data-in-recent-days-better and https://trello.com/c/W96ocnI5/663-daily-new-cases-handle-anomalous-trailing-zeros-better and is a first basic attempt at https://trello.com/c/Cq2zNk2M/674-annotate-data-outliers-that-weve-flagged-in-the-ui

* Adds `class TailFilter` which looks for and removes suspiciously low recent values of a cumulative timeseries.
* Adds `AnnotationField` and `AnnotationType` as a way to tag a particular location, variable, date as a place where the data was modified.
* Uses the above to filter the cumulative timeseries put in combined datasets
* Writes the annotations to a new CSV during `data update`
* Adds a new command `run-bad-tails-filter` for testing the filter.

## Tested

### For [HHS Test Positivity: Handle bad data in recent days better](https://trello.com/c/UKy1yEtd/664-hhs-test-positivity-handle-bad-data-in-recent-days-better)

Checked out the data from ~Dec 8 where TN and VA were broken, than used `run-bad-tails-filter` to check what the filter would have done. It looks like the stalled values would have been removed. The other changes I saw when skimming through the diff looked reasonable.
```
git checkout 04885f796deebab7cc6ed1e607a080d4483bff6a -- data/multiregion.csv data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv data/multiregion-static.csv data/multiregion-provenance.csv
./run.py data run-bad-tails-filter data/multiregion-wide-dates-bad-tails-filter.csv 
vimdiff data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv data/multiregion-wide-dates-bad-tails-filter.csv
```

### For [Daily New Cases: Handle anomalous trailing zeros better](https://trello.com/c/W96ocnI5/663-daily-new-cases-handle-anomalous-trailing-zeros-better)

Tested by checking out the data from snapshot 1413 with `git checkout 8beea39fc37ffb246f6e9f3299ba54071118685f -- data/` then running `./run.py data run-bad-tails-filter data/multiregion-wide-dates-bad-tails-filter.csv` and comparing with `vimdiff data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv data/multiregion-wide-dates-bad-tails-filter.csv` which shows that lots of bad tails were removed, including one value from NM cases. This is confirmed by looking at `grep us-nm,cases data/multiregion-wide-dates-bad-tails-filter-annotations.csv` which outputs `iso1:us#iso2:us-nm,cases,cumulative_tail_truncated,Removed 1 values less than 20.,2020-12-07`

author: Brett Boval <brettboval@gmail.com>
message:
Fix ICU Utilization Metric When Incorporating New 'Cumulative ICU' Datastream (#427)

Updated the 'estimate current number of hospital/icu beds occupied' by improving the model initialization and removing some unplanned sources of variability.

* ICU Estimation from Cumulative ICU Data

Improve the estimation of current icu covid patients in the case where we are only provided with cumulative icu patients.

Sometimes covidtracking provides cumulative, but not current, data for hospitalization and icu. We then estimate the number of patients currently in the ICU. There are multiple things with this implementation that need to be improved, however they can be done in stages. The first stage is to standardize the calculation of ICU. Right now the estimate uses a variable drawn from a wide distribution (roughly 8.6 +/- 2.6 days). This introduces a large source of noise in the snapshot to snapshot calculations. In other places this code is usually called multiple times and then averaged, but for here it is just called once. Instead of bumping up the call/average, I just calculated the value from the means. The consistancy day-to-day is key, especially since this parameter isn't used in any monte-carlo modeling.

I left the hospitilization branch still drawing from the distribution, but averaging over 250 samples. Timeit shows an increase from 8.4ms to 27.2ms. If this becomes significant, we can refactor the params code and surface this constant.

Finally, our new linter just came online, so there will be misc line cleanups for a bit.

* Parameter Scope Reduction for Temporary Test

The added parameter tripped up code elsewhere that has a script list of allowed keys. This constant is now local, but will be incorporated into the params later.

* Refactoring Current_To_Cumulative Code

Trying to isolate the code that converts current to cumulative from the code that just loads any data.

* Refactored Current to Cumulative Outside Load Data

Extracted the logic to convert cumulative totals to an estimate of current patient population. Before this, it was added into a data loading function as an optional flag. That structure was too constraining to include required features of the model (i.e. requiring more than one value provided to extrapolate from).

* Documentation and Reformatting

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
drop staffed_beds, regions without population (#831)

## This PR

* Adds call to `timeseries.drop_regions_without_population` which removes AS, GU, VI and Unknown Counties from combined data. Fixes `test_generate_infection_rate_metric_fake_fips` which was broken by the change.
* Removes `staffed_beds` from combined data. It is the only static metric that is build from a timeseries data source and removing it simplifies disentangling these
* Writes a copy of the static data next to the wide-dates csv. Unlike the latest.csv this includes regions without FIPS.
* Changes `add_new_cases` to use timeseries_wide_dates so that it produces identical results even if some dates with NA values for cases are removed
* Factors out the interesting parts of `MultiRegionDataset.from_timeseries_and_latest` so it is easier to remove.  Changes a bunch of tests in test/libs/datasets/timeseries_test.py to stop using `TimeseriesDataset` and `LatestValuesDataset` because they are about to be removed

## Tested

Ran `time ./run.py data update` and looked at `git difftool -t vimdiff data/multiregion.csv` to verify that the expected changes, and no more, took place.

message:
Remove Out of Date Data Disclaimers (#1330)

I audited the data disclaimers and found the following that should be removed:

- Louisiana state and sub-regions references a hurricane from 13 months ago
- Hawaii has duplicate overrides that are completely redundant
- Minnesota has a disclaimer that is not noticeable in the data (as currently masked)
- Idaho has caught up on the case backlog from earlier in the year
- Wisconsin has caught up on the case backlog from earlier in the year

Notes:

- I tested these changes out in the covid-projections frontend. There is a github action that copies the file from covid-data-model to covid-projections when building a new snapshot. So I am copying those local changes back over to this repo and committing them here to be rolled up in the next update.
- I only looked at non-blocking data disclaimers. To test the ongoing data blocks (such as vaccination data from Hawaii) would require rebuilding an api snapshot, which was out of scope for today.

author: Tom Brown <tom@covidactnow.org>
message:
test positivity copies tags to provide provenance output (#883)

## This PR

* Adds support for writing and reading multiple provenance values for a single timeseries
* Sorts tags by content as well as index, simplifying comparisons between datasets
* Fixes `combined_datasets` bug with missing provenance causing KeyError in loc
* Changes test positivity code to only copy tags from source columns. This removes the clunky way we were copying the method name to provenance
* Removes `wide_dates_df` because all the interesting code is in MultiRegionDataset now.
* Adds test_helper support for multiple provenance and build_default_region_dataset start_date

## Tested

```
git checkout main
python ./run.py api generate-test-positivity --output-dir results/output-main/
git checkout tgb-tag-combine-populate
mkdir results/output-tgb-tag-combine-populate
python ./run.py api generate-test-positivity --output-dir results/output-tgb-tag-combine-populate
```

Diff of `results/output-main/test-positivity-output.csv` is DC county (`iso1:us#iso2:us-dc#fips:11001`) lost its provenance because it uses aggregation which doesn't forward tags. It was `SmoothedTests` which isn't in TestPositivityRatioMethod so likely already broken.

Diff of `results/output-main/test-positivity-all.csv` is a bunch of states (AK, FL, OH, OK, OR, TX, UT, ....) going from positiveTestsViral_totalTestsViral to covid_tracking, likely an improvement. Plus the DC change above.

In main `results/output-main/test-positivity-output-annotations.csv` is empty but with this change it has 128 rows of suspicious observations removed, mostly counties, mostly 1 or 2 a location, lots in AR and TX.

message:
drop NYT for 6 MO counties (#1119)

This PR addresses https://trello.com/c/6roEMYkZ/1020-switch-to-usa-facts-for-6-mo-counties-nyt-is-under-reporting-kc-joplin-data

### Tested

```
./run.py data update
git difftool --no-prompt -t vimdiff main -- data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv
```

cbsa:27900 (Joplin) cumulative cases increased from 14.8k to 20.9k, an increase that matches number of cases in the city at https://www.joplinmo.org/1072/Joplins-CoronavirusCOVID-19-Response

fips:29037 (Cass), fips:29047 (Clay), fips:29145 (Newton), fips:29165 (Platte): source changed from NYT to USAFacts. Cases and deaths are pretty much unchanged.

fips:29097 (Jasper) changed source and counts increased a lot (cases 9.5k to 15.6k). It looks like USAFacts added all the city of Joplin counts to this county.

fips:29095 (Jackson) changed source and cases and deaths slightly more than doubled. I'm guessing USAFacts added all the Kansas City counts to this county.

author: Tristan <tristan.sebens@Wostmann.com>
message:
Fixed the missing backfill dates problem

Swapped the order of the cutoff and the backfill functions in the data
prep step.

The problem was being caused by holes in the data. If there is data on
feb 1, but nothing else until mar 10, then the backfill function will do
nothing because there's data prior to the cutoff date, then the cutoff
function will remove the feb data and the first date left will be the
10th. Now we cutoff first and backfill second.

author: Michael Lehenbauer <mikelehen@gmail.com>
message:
Estimate 1st dose data if it's been missing recently.

Previously we wouldn't estimate 1st dose data from completed if there was any
1st dose data at all.

With this change, we look back 16 days and if there's no 1st dose data in that
span, then we estimate 1st dose from completed. This is necessary since some
of the new CDC timeseries data has stale 1st dose data for some reason and we

This is some more cleanup associated with https://github.com/covid-projections/covid-data-model/pull/1094

* Adds tag parameter `Derived.f` to save the function name, useful now that we're adding that tag to the same field from multiple places.
* Replaces some direct access to `MultiRegionDataset.timeseries_bucketed_wide_dates` with new function `get_timeseries_bucketed_wide_dates` that returns one field and similarly for `timeseries_not_bucketed_wide_dates`.
* Replaces some calls to Index.get_level_values with Index.unique where a copy of the value per index entry isn't needed. See https://stackoverflow.com/a/50364903

## Tested

```
./run.py data update
git difftool --no-prompt -t vimdiff main -- data/multiregion-wide-dates.csv
```

Keep least stale vaccine percentage (#1090)

This PR is part of https://trello.com/c/tNlZtGp6/1279-make-our-vaccine-backfill-code-smarter

* Changes `vaccine_backfills.derive_vaccine_pct` to replace existing percentage metrics when the percentage derived from the people count has a real value on a more recent date

## Tested

I hacked in a change to write a wide-dates csv of the dataset before and after this change.
For counties in MD this adds a few days of data to `vaccinations_completed_pct` , for counties in ME this adds about 20 days of data to `vaccinations_initiated_pct`. It looks like the corresponding CBSAs had similar changes.

"Image must be nonzero".

author: Philip Cook <cookpa@pennmedicine.upenn.edu>
message:
WIP: buildx Docker CI with Github Actions (#369)

* WIP: buildx Docker CI with Github Actions

The Dockerfile would not build because of outdated CMake.

I first tried to install CMake via apt, but this failed because it required libssl1.0.0, and
the container OS only had libssl1.1.0.

Installing a new CMake from Kitware's binary installer worked.

Other changes:

 - Use the anaconda base image continuumio/miniconda3
 - Base the install layer off the smaller "debian:bullseye-slim"
 - Set default number of threads (2) to match Github runner

If there are any strange errors with the slim container, we may need to revert to the full "debian:bullseye".

            when None is provided and would pass this to the registration.  this

            prefer no mask at all.  As such, we no longer pass the mask to the
            registration when None is provided.
